events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception: July 30, 6 to 9pm Show Dates: July 30 thru August 24, 11am to 7pm Immersive Worlds: Cities, Castles and Countrysides Explore the many worlds we inhabit, real and fantastical. Curated by North Pole Artist Max LaZebnik, this exhibition draws deeply from North Pole Studio’s archive to present a compelling selection of works that examine the spaces, landscapes, and communities that shape our sense of belonging. Moving between urban centers, fantastical structures, and rural environments, the featured works invite viewers to consider how meaning is constructed through place. North Pole Studio supports careers in the arts and exists to increase opportunities for artists with autism and intellectual/developmental disabilities to thrive as active members of the arts community. It fosters self-determination and facilitates meaningful connections through total engagement in the arts. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.
events.title: Immersive Worlds: Cities, Castles and Countrysides

events.summary: Chefas Projects is delighted to welcome back sculptor Jessie Weitzel Le Grand for her fourth exhibition with the gallery entitled Astral Accessories. Communication arrives fractured: as static, interference, intuition, and half-remembered technologies that once promised connection. In Astral Accessories, Portland-based artist Jessie Weitzel Le Grand presents a new body of sculptural work that imagines obsolete technological devices as enigmatic relics from alternate realities. Equal parts artifact, machine, and living organism, the sculptures transform familiar forms into mysterious conduits for uncertainty, speculation, and wonder. Drawing on the visual language of outdated communications technology, the exhibition considers what remains when systems of transmission fail or become obsolete. Unmanageable and invisible, signals continue to pass through space, whirring beyond perception, like sirens too quiet to hear. Meaning emerges imperfectly through noise, distortion, and interruption, where messages are received as static, interference, and fragmented memory rather than clear transmission. Rather than offering resolution, Astral Accessories embraces ambiguity. The works suggest speculative tools for communicating across impossible distances: between worlds, across time, or with forms of intelligence that remain just beyond comprehension. Suspended between archaeology and science fiction, the sculptures ask viewers to reconsider the objects that mediate our relationships with technology, memory, and the unknown. Utilizing an eclectic array of materials, including ceramics, thermoplastic, flashe paint, and even materials used in fly tying, Weitzel Le Grand blurs the boundaries between art, artifact, and technology. Interested in exploring how we perceive reality and questioning the certainty of what we see, she embeds natural elements such as orchids, moths, and fragments of coral within computer motherboards, rotary telephones, and other obsolete technologies in disorienting, exuberant configurations. By reimagining these nostalgic devices in playful yet unfamiliar ways, she encourages viewers to question their function and invent their own narratives around the mysterious systems they seem to inhabit. By transforming obsolete technologies into uncanny relics, Weitzel Le Grand creates a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and failed technologies become vessels for new forms of connection. Jessie Weitzel Le Grand (b. 1987) was born and raised in Portland, Oregon, where she continues to live and work. She received a BFA from the Pacific Northwest College of Art and an MAT from Marylhurst University. Her work has recently been exhibited at Galerie Lefebvre & Fils (Paris, France), Outback Arthouse (Los Angeles, California), Oregon Contemporary (Portland, Oregon), and as part of Lazy Oaf's Take A Break exhibition (London, United Kingdom). She is the co-founder of carnation Contemporary, a collective of emerging and mid-career artists from the Pacific Northwest championing critical contemporary art, and Well Well Projects, an artist-member gallery in Portland's Kenton neighborhood. In 2025, she was featured in Create! Magazine Issue #49 and is currently represented by Chefas Projects.
events.title: JESSIE WEITZEL LE GRAND | ASTRAL ACCESSORIES

events.summary: Chefas Projects is pleased to present Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, San Francisco–based artist Lindsay Stripling's debut solo exhibition with the gallery. Through luminous watercolor paintings, Stripling creates dreamlike worlds where memory, intuition, and the rhythms of the natural world converge. Her imagined landscapes and nature-infused portraits blur the boundaries between observation and imagination, inviting viewers into spaces where storytelling becomes a means of navigating identity, belonging, and transformation. Rooted in experimentation, texture, and play, Stripling's practice embraces watercolor as both a precise and unpredictable medium. Layers of transparent color accumulate into richly atmospheric compositions that evoke fleeting memories, quiet psychological states, and the mysterious logic of dreams. Plants, animals, and human figures coexist in environments that feel at once deeply familiar and gently surreal, suggesting a world in which the human experience is inseparable from the more-than-human landscape. Throughout Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, Stripling explores themes of nature, time, community, psychology, and personal mythology. Rather than offering fixed narratives, her paintings unfold as open-ended visual poems, encouraging viewers to project their own memories and emotional landscapes into the work. Each composition balances meticulous craftsmanship with a spirit of curiosity, revealing beauty in uncertainty and wonder in the everyday. The exhibition's title poses a deceptively simple question, one that gestures toward the unseen journeys taking place beyond the limits of perception. Like migratory paths traced through darkness, Stripling's paintings invite contemplation of the invisible forces that shape our relationships with ourselves, one another, and the natural world. Lindsay Stripling is a San Francisco–based painter, illustrator, and educator. Working primarily in watercolor, she explores the intersections of storytelling, memory, dreams, and ecology through richly layered paintings that combine intimate portraiture with expansive natural imagery. Where Do Geese Fly at Night? marks her first solo exhibition with Chefas Projects.
events.title: LINDSAY STRIPLING | WHERE DO GEESE FLY AT NIGHT?

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. events.summary: Join Argentine classical guitarist Luciano Marazzo for an intimate evening of music celebrating the rich traditions of Latin American and Spanish guitar. The repertoire blends Argentine dances, modern tango, and beloved masterpieces of the Spanish guitar tradition. The concert takes place at the beautiful Mars House in Portland, a warm and inspiring cultural space known for its welcoming atmosphere and close connection between audience and performer. With seating for around 50 guests, this event offers a rare opportunity to experience classical guitar up close in an intimate setting. Come enjoy an evening of expressive music, storytelling, and some of the most captivating works in the guitar repertoire. 🎟 Tickets required — limited seating available.

events.summary: TICKETS truewest.info/GWDR-26 On Sale Friday, May 15 at 10am PT This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- Gillian Welch and David Rawlings are pillars of the modern acoustic music world and their rich and remarkable careers span over twenty-five years. They have been hailed by Pitchfork as “modern masters of American folk” and “protectors of the American folk song” by Rolling Stone and the New York Times says “their combined voices operate beyond simple sonic harmony. There are emotional inquiries at play. If Welch’s voice delivers the good news or the hard news of the world, Rawlings’s voice comes underneath, asking how much deeper the sadness can go or what fresh heights the ecstatic can climb to.” Their most recent 10th studio album, Woodland, won the 2025 Best Folk Album GRAMMY. Woodland was named for and recorded at Welch and Rawlings’ own Woodland Sound Studios in Nashville, TN. Of the album and studio, Welch said, “Woodland is at the heart of everything we do and has been for the last twenty some years. The past four years were spent almost entirely within its walls, bringing it back to life after the 2020 tornado and making this record. The music is \(songs are\) a swirl of contradictions, emptiness, fullness, joy, grief, destruction, permanence. Now.” The new 10-song collection mingles full band tracks with intricate duet performances all tied together with the duo’s signature sound and lyricism and cements the pair’s iconoclastic position at the forefront of acoustic music. After moving to Nashville in the 1990s, Welch was launched into the public consciousness when Emmylou Harris recorded a cover of Welch’s “Orphan Girl.” Her career continued to flourish as her 1996 debut Revival, produced by T Bone Burnett, was released to critical acclaim. Firmly on the roots music map following the release, Welch and Rawlings followed up that GRAMMY nominated album release with 1998’s Hell Among The Yearlings, a stark duet record that further solidified the duo as a force in the folk music scene

What initially seems like a mere publicity stunt soon becomes a soul-baring battle of wills. Only one can win, but for all involved, the truck holds the key to their own private American dream. The mix of people in this contest includes: an unlikeable prior winner who is a bit racist; the son of an immigrant who wants to be a veterinarian; a USMC veteran; an older woman (with her husband for support) who really needs the money; a Texas evangelical; a beauty queen; an older man (and his wife as support) who is recovering from a fall from a big rig; and a few other folks. We‘re celebrating the album release at their home venue (and where the album was recorded)— the goodfoot. Joining before and in between their sets will be local techno legend leeonn. Expect nearly five hours of continuous music (starting as soon as the doors open at 9pm) !Led by bassist Brett McConnell since 2017, the band features a unique sound of electronic drums, multiple synths, two basses, lap steel guitar, and the inimitable Aniana on vocals. events.summary: Instrumental delivery can be a necessary medical intervention during childbirth, but when forceps or a vacuum extractor are used incorrectly, mothers may suffer serious physical and emotional harm. Injuries such as severe perineal tears, pelvic floor damage, nerve injuries, excessive bleeding, or long-term pain can have lasting effects on daily life. If these injuries resulted from avoidable medical errors or substandard care, the affected mother may have grounds to pursue a compensation claim. Establishing negligence typically requires evidence that healthcare professionals failed to meet the accepted standard of care and that this directly caused the injury. Every case is unique, so medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the delivery are carefully evaluated. Claims can help recover compensation for medical expenses, rehabilitation, lost income, ongoing care, and pain and suffering. The physical and emotional Traume from Instrumental Delivery may also be considered when assessing the full impact of the injury on the mother's quality of life. Understanding your legal rights is an important first step toward seeking justice. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance to individuals who believe their injuries were caused by negligent medical treatment. Their experience in investigating childbirth-related negligence helps clients understand whether they have a valid claim and what legal options may be available. Seeking legal advice promptly can also help preserve important evidence and ensure claims are brought within the applicable time limits.
events.title: Maternal injuries during instrumental delivery lead to compensation claims?

events.summary: Proving a Surgical Negligence claim requires strong, well-documented evidence that demonstrates how a healthcare provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and caused avoidable harm. Medical records are often the foundation of the case, providing a detailed timeline of diagnosis, treatment, surgery, and follow-up care. Expert medical opinions are equally important because they help establish whether the surgeon's actions fell below the standard expected of a reasonably competent professional. Diagnostic scans, laboratory results, surgical notes, consent forms, and hospital records can further support the claim. Witness statements from medical professionals or others involved in the patient's care may also strengthen the evidence. It is essential to show not only that an error occurred but also that the mistake directly resulted in physical, emotional, or financial damage. Documentation of ongoing treatment, rehabilitation, lost income, and future medical needs can help demonstrate the full impact of the injury. Every case is unique, making a thorough investigation critical before legal proceedings begin. An experienced solicitor can identify the evidence needed, obtain independent expert reports, and build a compelling legal argument. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases and understands the detailed approach required to investigate Surgical Negligence claims. Their experience in reviewing medical evidence and working with independent experts helps clients present well-supported claims. By carefully gathering relevant documentation and establishing causation, they aim to protect the rights of individuals affected by avoidable surgical errors. Seeking legal guidance early can also help preserve important evidence and ensure procedural deadlines are met. A well-prepared case supported by credible evidence significantly improves the likelihood of achieving a fair outcome.
events.title: What evidence is required to prove a surgical negligence claim?

events.summary: When parents suspect that a birth injury could have been prevented, taking prompt and informed action is essential. The first step is to seek appropriate medical care for the child and ensure that all ongoing health concerns are properly documented. Parents should also request copies of medical records, including labour, delivery, and neonatal care notes, as these documents may help clarify what happened during childbirth. It is often beneficial to keep a detailed record of symptoms, treatments, and conversations with healthcare providers. In some situations, concerns may arise about Traume from Instrumental Delivery, particularly if forceps or a vacuum extractor were used during a difficult birth and the child later developed injuries. While not every complication is the result of negligence, a thorough legal review can determine whether accepted medical standards were followed. Understanding the cause of a birth injury can help families make informed decisions about their next steps. Experienced legal professionals can explain the claims process, the evidence required, and the applicable time limits without creating unnecessary stress for parents. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on medical negligence cases, including birth injury claims, and provides guidance to families seeking answers after a traumatic delivery. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters can help parents understand whether avoidable errors may have contributed to their child's injuries. Taking early action also helps preserve important evidence and protects a family's legal rights. Most importantly, parents should remember that seeking legal advice is not only about pursuing compensation but also about obtaining accountability and securing support for their child's future care and long-term needs.
events.title: What should parents do if they suspect birth trauma was avoidable?

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: Medical experts play a crucial role in evaluating injuries that occur during assisted childbirth by carefully reviewing medical records, delivery notes, imaging scans, and the condition of both the mother and baby. They assess whether forceps, vacuum extraction, or other assisted delivery methods were used appropriately according to accepted medical standards. Specialists also examine the timing of interventions, fetal monitoring records, and whether alternative delivery options should have been considered. Their findings help determine if the injuries resulted from unavoidable complications or preventable medical negligence. In cases involving Traume from Instrumental Delivery, experts evaluate the extent of physical and neurological harm, the expected long-term impact, and the treatment or rehabilitation that may be required. They may consult with obstetricians, pediatric neurologists, radiologists, and rehabilitation professionals to provide an objective medical opinion. This expert evidence is often essential in establishing whether the standard of care fell below what would reasonably be expected. A detailed medical assessment can also help quantify the financial and personal impact of the injury, including ongoing healthcare needs and loss of quality of life. Families seeking answers often rely on experienced legal professionals to interpret these findings within the context of a compensation claim. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases, including those involving assisted childbirth injuries, and works closely with independent medical experts to build well-supported claims. By combining detailed medical evidence with legal expertise, the firm helps clients understand their rights and pursue fair compensation where negligence has contributed to avoidable birth injuries.

events.summary: Surgical negligence under Irish law occurs when a surgeon, hospital, or other healthcare professional fails to provide the standard of care that a reasonably competent medical practitioner would have delivered in similar circumstances, resulting in avoidable harm to a patient. This can include operating on the wrong site, causing preventable surgical injuries, failing to obtain informed consent, leaving surgical instruments inside the body, or providing inadequate post-operative care. Every case is assessed on its own facts, and proving Surgical Negligence generally requires evidence showing that the accepted standard of medical care was breached and that the breach directly caused the injury. Patients may experience additional medical treatment, prolonged recovery, financial losses, or long-term physical and emotional effects because of negligent surgical care. Irish law allows eligible patients to seek compensation where negligence can be established through appropriate medical and legal evidence. Understanding your legal rights early can make a significant difference in protecting your interests and preserving important evidence. Seeking advice from experienced legal professionals helps clarify whether the circumstances meet the legal threshold for Surgical Negligence. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on representing clients in complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance throughout the legal process with a clear understanding of Irish medical negligence law. Their experience in handling surgical negligence cases helps clients understand the evidence required, the claims process, and the potential outcomes. Whether the issue involves a surgical error, delayed treatment after surgery, or another avoidable complication, obtaining informed legal advice is an important first step toward pursuing justice and fair compensation.
events.title: What is considered surgical negligence under Irish law?

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

Curated by North Pole Artist Max LaZebnik, this exhibition draws deeply from North Pole Studio’s archive to present a compelling selection of works that examine the spaces, landscapes, and communities that shape our sense of belonging. Moving between urban centers, fantastical structures, and rural environments, the featured works invite viewers to consider how meaning is constructed through place. North Pole Studio supports careers in the arts and exists to increase opportunities for artists with autism and intellectual/developmental disabilities to thrive as active members of the arts community. It fosters self-determination and facilitates meaningful connections through total engagement in the arts. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.
events.title: Immersive Worlds: Cities, Castles and Countrysides

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception: July 30, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: July 30 thru August 24. Botanical Alchemy Experience the alchemical marriage of Mary Lyn Gough’s earthen floral watercolors and Kirra Teal Hellfritsch’s metamorphic jewelry. Together, their work explores the transformation of the natural world through elemental materials and traditional craftsmanship. Rooted in botanical forms and natural processes, both artists celebrate the enduring beauty found within growth, decay, and renewal. Their work reveals the quiet magic of nature translated through paint and metal.
events.title: Botanical Alchemy: Jewelry and Watercolor

events.summary: The Portland Go Club provides interactive teachings on the rules, strategies, and history of Weiqi. 11 AM – 1 PM | Every 3rd Sunday, April 19 – September 20, 2026 Weiqi, also known as Go, holds the distinction of being the oldest continuously played strategy game globally, with origins dating back at least 3,500 years. While its rules can be grasped in mere minutes, the game’s strategies and historical significance are vast. As part of our ongoing cultural programs, the Portland Go Club will provide teachings and demonstrations on the rules, strategies, and history of Weiqi, considered one of the four traditional Scholarly Arts. Attendees will have the opportunity to observe live demonstrations and engage in Weiqi gameplay with volunteers from the Portland Go Club. Get Admission About the Portland Go Club The Portland Go Club, established in 1977, has been facilitating Go/Weiqi meetups and events for nearly 50 years in the Portland area. The club hosts two weekly gatherings for players of all skill levels to play and learn about the game and its strategies. PGC hosts various community events including an annual Statewide tournament, workshops taught by Professional Weiqi players, educational tabling at cultural events, and workshops for new players. We welcome players of all experience levels and are happy to teach new players at any of our meetups. Learn more Parking & Directions Free Lan Su Parking There is free first come, first served parking in our sister lot next to the garden at 424 NW Third Avenue. Additional metered parking and garages are available on surrounding streets.
events.title: Weiqi/Go Teaching and Demonstrating

events.summary: The Rockstar Energy Open is set to return, electrifying downtown Portland, Oregon at Tom McCall Waterfront Park from August 14–16, 2026. Now in its third year, the free, three-day spectacle unites the next generation of skateboarding phenoms with world-class legends —bringing fans a high-impact weekend built to bring the Rockstar Energy Live Loud™ identity to life, where skateboarding, music and culture collide. events.summary: Few people knew John Lennon as intimately as May Pang. Pang was Lennon’s lover during the infamous “Lost Weekend” which lasted 18 months during late 1973 through 1975. A collection of these private photographs will be on display and available for purchase at The Lawrence Gallery, 540 N. State St, Lake Oswego on Friday, August 14 - Sunday, August 16. All works are available to purchase - See John Lennon as May saw him! events.title: The Lost Weekend - The Photography of May Pang

events.summary: Climb aboard for a memorable rail adventure through the heart of Portland! The Oregon Rail Heritage Center’s popular weekend train rides return May 23 through October 11, 2026, with departures every Saturday and Sunday behind historic diesel locomotive BNSF 3613. Perfect for families, visitors, and train lovers of all ages, these scenic excursions offer a unique way to experience Portland from the rails. Passengers can ride in an open-air car or relax in a vintage air-conditioned coach while taking in views of Portland’s skyline, the riverfront, local wildlife, and the timeless charm of Oaks Park. Your ticket also includes admission to the Oregon Rail Heritage Center, where guests can explore Portland’s rich rail history and see historic locomotives up close. Whether it’s your first train ride or a favorite family tradition, this classic Portland experience is one you won’t want to miss! When: Saturdays & Sundays, May 23 – October 11, 2026 Where: Oregon Rail Heritage Center, 2250 SE Water Ave., Portland, OR, 97214 Ticket Prices: • Adults (14+): $17 • Children (3–13): $12 • Seniors (65+) & Military: $15 • Family Pass: $50 (2 adults + 2 children) • Infants under 3 ride free on a lap Advance ticket purchase is recommended. Service charges apply. Please arrive at least 20 minutes before departure for check-in and boarding.
events.title: Weekend Train Rides at the Oregon Rail Heritage Center

events.summary: This summer, a multi-sensory art experience called Shifting Realities will take over Porsche Studio Portland for a creative journey produced by artists from Portland and across the country. The space turns into a living canvas where you don’t just observe the work, you become part of it. Across multiple interactive environments, you’ll see sound take physical form, design in real time using light and gesture, and step into spaces that respond to your movement, energy, and input. From large-scale visual installations to hands-on creative moments and a multisensory tasting experience, each part of the experience is designed to blur the line between artist and audience. Guests move through the experience in timed groups, progressing together through each space while still having room to explore and interact along the way. Running June 4 through August 31, Shifting Realities is a 100 minute limited-run installation that’s built for all ages and occasions. Tickets start at $39 ($41.34 incl. fees), with reduced pricing for kids and options for VIP, private, and group bookings.
events.title: Shifting Realities: A New Immersive Art Exhibition at Porsche Studio

events.summary: When an auto dealership in Longview, TX, launches an endurance contest, ten economically strapped strangers embark on a journey that tests their hearts, minds, and bodies. The contestant who keeps at least one hand on a brand-new hardbody truck the longest gets to drive it off the lot. What initially seems like a mere publicity stunt soon becomes a soul-baring battle of wills. Only one can win, but for all involved, the truck holds the key to their own private American dream. The mix of people in this contest includes: an unlikeable prior winner who is a bit racist; the son of an immigrant who wants to be a veterinarian; a USMC veteran; an older woman (with her husband for support) who really needs the money; a Texas evangelical; a beauty queen; an older man (and his wife as support) who is recovering from a fall from a big rig; and a few other folks. The backstory involves the faltering dealership, lack of sales, and unethical behavior by some of the staff.
events.title: Hands On A Hard Body

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season

events.summary: TICKETS truewest.info/GWDR-26 On Sale Friday, May 15 at 10am PT This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- Gillian Welch and David Rawlings are pillars of the modern acoustic music world and their rich and remarkable careers span over twenty-five years. They have been hailed by Pitchfork as “modern masters of American folk” and “protectors of the American folk song” by Rolling Stone and the New York Times says “their combined voices operate beyond simple sonic harmony. There are emotional inquiries at play. If Welch’s voice delivers the good news or the hard news of the world, Rawlings’s voice comes underneath, asking how much deeper the sadness can go or what fresh heights the ecstatic can climb to.” Their most recent 10th studio album, Woodland, won the 2025 Best Folk Album GRAMMY. Woodland was named for and recorded at Welch and Rawlings’ own Woodland Sound Studios in Nashville, TN. Of the album and studio, Welch said, “Woodland is at the heart of everything we do and has been for the last twenty some years. The past four years were spent almost entirely within its walls, bringing it back to life after the 2020 tornado and making this record. The music is \(songs are\) a swirl of contradictions, emptiness, fullness, joy, grief, destruction, permanence. Now.” The new 10-song collection mingles full band tracks with intricate duet performances all tied together with the duo’s signature sound and lyricism and cements the pair’s iconoclastic position at the forefront of acoustic music. After moving to Nashville in the 1990s, Welch was launched into the public consciousness when Emmylou Harris recorded a cover of Welch’s “Orphan Girl.” Her career continued to flourish as her 1996 debut Revival, produced by T Bone Burnett, was released to critical acclaim. Firmly on the roots music map following the release, Welch and Rawlings followed up that GRAMMY nominated album release with 1998’s Hell Among The Yearlings, a stark duet record that further solidified the duo as a force in the folk music scene
events.title: Gillian Welch & David Rawlings play Grateful Dead acoustic Reckoning

events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/OBrien26 On Sale Friday, May 29 at 10am PT This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- This summer, Olivia O’Brien will step back into the light with her highly anticipated sophomore album, PIXIE. The 15-track project showcases her strongest and most honest songwriting yet, presaging this chapter as her most authentic and assured to date. With over 2.3 billion aggregate global streams, Olivia O’Brien has built a catalog that continues to resonate with listeners around the world. She first gained widespread attention with her cover of Avril Levigne’s “complicated,” which amassed over 388 million streams. Just a year later, she released “hate u love u” alongside gnash, a breakout hit that has surpassed 1.5 billion global streams, peaked at \#10 on the Billboard Hot 100, and earned RIAA Gold certification. Olivia later released a version featuring just her vocals, which accrued over 490 million Spotify streams and further cemented the song as one of the defining pop records of its era. In 2020, Olivia’s emotionally charged breakup anthem “Josslyn” became another watershed moment in her career, amassing over 220 million streams, and paving the way for appearances on culturally lauded podcasts like Call Her Daddy and The Zach Sang Show. Her work and trajectory have been profiled extensively by publications like NYLON, Billboard, COVETEUR, and PAPER, among others. In 2024, Olivia’s EP everywhere i go, there i am represented a creative turning point in her career, shifting from traditional pop to a more textured, indie-leaning sound. The project examines the growing pains of early adulthood, internal contradiction, and the old versions of ourselves that we shed with age, and signified a new commitment to creating music that fully reflected Olivia’s own identity and artistic agency. With PIXIE, Olivia O’Brien turns the page with clarity and conviction, stepping into a chapter that feels less like a reinvention and more like a true arrival

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org

events.summary: This summer, Portland Japanese Garden is host to a glowing world of light. Woven Light showcases the illuminated washi sculptures of Yuri Kinoshita, a Seattle-based artist who artfully crafts floating landscapes of light through her sculptural lamps that bridge the art and design world. Guests who visit the Calvin and Mayho Tanabe Gallery will see that through carefully hand-woven and sculpted washi (Japanese handmade paper made from plant fibers), soft light and shadow inspire a magical sense of place, evoking the unique environment of the Pacific Northwest. More than artwork, Kinoshita’s works are experiences that transport the viewer into a warm world of light through both works that evoke natural forms and abstracted shapes that inspire contemplation.

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception: July 30, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: July 30 thru August 24. Botanical Alchemy Experience the alchemical marriage of Mary Lyn Gough’s earthen floral watercolors and Kirra Teal Hellfritsch’s metamorphic jewelry. Together, their work explores the transformation of the natural world through elemental materials and traditional craftsmanship. Rooted in botanical forms and natural processes, both artists celebrate the enduring beauty found within growth, decay, and renewal. Their work reveals the quiet magic of nature translated through paint and metal.

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception: July 30, 6 to 9pm Show Dates: July 30 thru August 24, 11am to 7pm Immersive Worlds: Cities, Castles and Countrysides Explore the many worlds we inhabit, real and fantastical. Curated by North Pole Artist Max LaZebnik, this exhibition draws deeply from North Pole Studio’s archive to present a compelling selection of works that examine the spaces, landscapes, and communities that shape our sense of belonging. Moving between urban centers, fantastical structures, and rural environments, the featured works invite viewers to consider how meaning is constructed through place. North Pole Studio supports careers in the arts and exists to increase opportunities for artists with autism and intellectual/developmental disabilities to thrive as active members of the arts community. It fosters self-determination and facilitates meaningful connections through total engagement in the arts. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.
events.title: Immersive Worlds: Cities, Castles and Countrysides

events.summary: Join us Mondays this summer for a generative freewriting session. This group will be led by author Dian Greenwood. Each session will begin with a writing prompt, then dedicated writing time, followed by time for willing participants to share what they wrote. Meet other writers in a friendly space, explore your own craft, and be surprised at what your mind creates with a prompt and time to write. This group is open to writers of all levels and is a supportive environment. Dian Greenwood studied writing \(emphasis on poetry\) at San Francisco State University. She later studied novel writing with Janet Fitch \(White Oleander\) and Tom Spanbauer \(In the City of Shy Hunters\). Dian published About the Carleton Sisters \(2023, She Writes Press\) at age 81 and, a year later, Forever Blackbirds \(2024\). The Blackbird sequel, Blackbird Whistling came out in September 2025, both books from Traveler’s Moon Press. Dian previously published essays in the online magazine, The Big Smoke, America. Her Substack essays can be found at It’s Never Too Late. Dian lives in Portland, Oregon, where she writes and works as a family therapist. Mondays, July 6, 13, 20, and 27; August 3, 10, 17, 24, 31 5:30–6:30 p.m. \(Arrive at 5:00 to order a drink and food and chat with other writers.\) FREE, $7 suggested donation for group leader \\\\\* Event cohosted by BOLD Coffee & Books and Indigo: Editing, Design, and More.

events.summary: TICKETS truewest.info/GWDR-26 On Sale Friday, May 15 at 10am PT This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- Gillian Welch and David Rawlings are pillars of the modern acoustic music world and their rich and remarkable careers span over twenty-five years. They have been hailed by Pitchfork as “modern masters of American folk” and “protectors of the American folk song” by Rolling Stone and the New York Times says “their combined voices operate beyond simple sonic harmony. There are emotional inquiries at play. If Welch’s voice delivers the good news or the hard news of the world, Rawlings’s voice comes underneath, asking how much deeper the sadness can go or what fresh heights the ecstatic can climb to.” Their most recent 10th studio album, Woodland, won the 2025 Best Folk Album GRAMMY. Woodland was named for and recorded at Welch and Rawlings’ own Woodland Sound Studios in Nashville, TN. Of the album and studio, Welch said, “Woodland is at the heart of everything we do and has been for the last twenty some years. The past four years were spent almost entirely within its walls, bringing it back to life after the 2020 tornado and making this record. The music is \(songs are\) a swirl of contradictions, emptiness, fullness, joy, grief, destruction, permanence. Now.” The new 10-song collection mingles full band tracks with intricate duet performances all tied together with the duo’s signature sound and lyricism and cements the pair’s iconoclastic position at the forefront of acoustic music. After moving to Nashville in the 1990s, Welch was launched into the public consciousness when Emmylou Harris recorded a cover of Welch’s “Orphan Girl.” Her career continued to flourish as her 1996 debut Revival, produced by T Bone Burnett, was released to critical acclaim. Firmly on the roots music map following the release, Welch and Rawlings followed up that GRAMMY nominated album release with 1998’s Hell Among The Yearlings, a stark duet record that further solidified the duo as a force in the folk music scene
events.title: Gillian Welch & David Rawlings play Grateful Dead acoustic Reckoning

events.summary: Acclaimed author and Pulitzer Prize winner Rae Armantrout's remarkable new collection, Safe Rooms \(Wesleyan University Press\), explores the undercurrents of modern life with an unflinching eye on human nature, social malaise, and the unsettling ways in which we attempt to protect ourselves from a world that continually undermines our sense of safety. As the title poem says: "your thoughts /roar and echo//around you—originating/god knows where.// You try to plug your ears/but you are an ear/ that can't stop listening." Through poems that examine our darker impulses — our tendencies to self-destruct, to grapple with envy, and to navigate the intricate web of family dynamics —Armantrout captures the complex, often contradictory ways in which we search for meaning and connection. Her work holds a mirror to the forces shaping us, both intimate and vast, showing that the so-called "safe rooms" we construct are fragile, temporary shelters, not havens from the chaos that surrounds us. Armantrout will be joined in conversation by poet John Beer, author of Lucinda. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/rae-armantrout-9780819502568
events.title: Powell's Presents: Rae Armantrout in Conversation With John Beer

events.summary: Melvin wants to clean up the most polluted town in New Jersey. But when the mayor's bullies dump him into a vat of radioactive toxic waste, he reemerges as The Toxic Avenger. Now, with superhuman strength and a heart as big as Newark, he's out to save New Jersey, end global warming, and find love. The Toxic Avenger is a charming, irreverent, hilarious love story with an unlikely hero, an aspiring author, a corrupt New Jersey mayor, bullies, mobsters, professors, folk singers, and more. Featuring a wailin' rock score, this comical musical has something for everyone to enjoy. ABOUT ANONYMOUS THEATRE Auditions are held... in secret. The play is cast... in secret. Cast members rehearse the show one-on-one with the director... secretly... and do not learn the identity of the other cast members. On the night of the performance, the actors arrive in street clothes and enter the theatre as if they are members of the audience. They take their seats. They read their programs. They chat with their neighbors. The house lights dim and the play begins... with each actor delivering his or her first line from their seat. The audience gets to see the story happen as if it is happening for the first time... because it actually is happening for the first time.
events.title: Anonymous Theatre: THE TOXIC AVENGER

events.summary: Part of the Hanabi Film Festival 2026. Limited festival passes available while supplies last. Doors open at 8:30 PM; film at 9:00 PM. When thief Birdey is caught stealing from a book shop by salesgirl Umeko, the two embark on an unusual, erotic adventure. Directed by Japanese New Wave legend Nagisa Ōshima \(Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence\) and co-written by close collaborator Mamoru Sasaki \(Death by Hanging\), the film sharply divided critics on its release and continues to perplex audiences today. The New York Times said the film had “an air of having been produced only for purposes of demonstration,” while the Guardian praised it as “an explosive agitprop movie equating sexual liberation with revolution.” Switching between color and black and white, coherent plot and pure vibes, Ōshima pushed the boundaries of the 1960s experimental, left-wing movement. Commonly referred to as “the Japanese Godard,” Ōshima said he preferred that Jean-Luc Godard be called “the French Ōshima.” Screened in Japanese with English subtitles. Director: Nagisa Ōshima Year: 1969 Country: Japan Runtime: 92 minutes

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present our summer group show Mixed Flock: 30 Years, marking the celebration of the gallery’s thirtieth anniversary. Mixed Flock comes from the idea of different species of birds gathering together for a variety of reasons including safety, cooperation, and community. In talking with wildlife scientist Derek Craighead about mixed flocks, Craighead suggested humans underestimate the sociability of animals, that wild animals will gather to be social, for fun, and for company. That’s worthwhile! For thirty years, PDX artist’s have been a wonderful mixed flock with each artist having their own way of seeing the world and approaching their art-making. Now is an important time to highlight and strengthen mixed flocks. Our country is a mixed flock, the “melting pot”, where diverse peoples, cultures, and ways exist together and we are better for it. This show is a celebration of the gallery’s many and varied artists, supporters, and collectors who make up our flock. Mixed Flock: 30 Years features work from represented and invited artists including: Anna Gray + Ryan Wilson Pauslen, Nick Blosser, Iván Carmona, Marjorie Dial, Amjad Faur, Bean Finneran, Jacques Flechemueller, Ellen George, Johannes GiararVictoria Haven, Elizabeth Knight, Justin L’Amie, Alma Allen, James Lavadour, Terran Last Gun, Nathan William Lambdin, Nancy Lorenz, Kristen Miller, Wes Mills, Jeffry Mitchell, Megan Murphy, Jenene Nagy, Ido Radon, Georgina Reskala, Joe Rudko, Tad Savinar, Susan Seubert, Adam Sorensen, Barbara Stafford, Storm Tharp, Gus Van Sant, Nell Warren, Heather Watkins, Marie Watt, and Yamamoto Masao.
events.title: Mixed Flock: 30 Years

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

Moving between urban centers, fantastical structures, and rural environments, the featured works invite viewers to consider how meaning is constructed through place. North Pole Studio supports careers in the arts and exists to increase opportunities for artists with autism and intellectual/developmental disabilities to thrive as active members of the arts community. It fosters self-determination and facilitates meaningful connections through total engagement in the arts. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season

events.summary: Following the breakout success of the bestselling What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking, Substack star Caroline Chambers returns with a new cookbook offering 100 more recipes for busy people who love good food — and these can be made even faster! Chambers famously doesn’t feel like cooking — and she’s built a whole brand on that premise. Her superpowers are eliminating unnecessary steps, minimizing dirty dishes, and making dinnertime as simple, stress-free, and fun as possible. While plenty of obstacles stand between you and a delicious meal, being short on time is probably the biggest one. Chambers’s exciting follow-up cookbook, What to Cook When You Don't Feel Like Cooking: Make It Fast \(Union Square & Co.\), is once again organized into three time-based chapters. You’ll find recipes for 100 dinners, all of which are complete meals and can be made with no more than 30 minutes hands-on time in the kitchen — and yes, that includes chopping, marinating, and all other prep! Every quick and easy recipe features Caro’s signature swaps, riffs, tips, and shortcuts to empower you to make these recipes work for you — not the other way around! You’ll also find special treasures throughout the book, including anchor recipes you can spin into five different dishes so you can DIY your favorites. Even on the nights when you think there’s no way, no how, What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking: Make It Fast will help you get a full, flavorful meal on the table in basically no time. Please note: This is a ticketed event. Tickets include admission, as well as one hardcover copy of What to Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking: Make It Fast. events.summary: The Breeders are an American rock band, formed in 1988 by Kim Deal of Pixies and Throwing Muses' Tanya Donelly. After those original bands became less active, The Breeders became more important to both artists. A tape was sent of their original demos to Ivo Watts-Russell, who immediately signed the band to his 4AD label in 1989. Their debut album, "Pod", was recorded by Steve Albini and released on 4AD in 1990. Deal's influence is obvious, but bassist Josephine Wiggs and Slint drummer Britt Walford \(credited here as Shannon Doughton\) add to the ensemble sound. By the release of the four-song EP "Safari" in 1992, Deal was done with Pixies and had enlisted her twin sister Kelley Deal to play guitar for the Breeders. Donelly exited the band to form Belly, and drummer Jim MacPherson joined in time for "Last Splash" in 1993. The album spawned the hit "Cannonball." In 1995, Kelley Deal was involved in a drug bust, so sister Kim formed the side project The Amps with MacPherson, bassist Luis Lerma \(member of Dayton, Ohio band The Tasties\) and guitarist Nate Farley, who later joined Guided by Voices. The Amps released the album "Pacer" in October of 1995. Following drug rehab, Kelley started the Kelley Deal 6000 and also formed the unlikely Last Hard Men with Skid Row singer Sebastian Bach, ex-The Smashing Pumpkins drummer Jimmy Chamberlin, and Jimmy Flemion of The Frogs. Rumours of Kim Deal reuniting with the original band continued to circulate in the 90s, although the only material to surface was a cover of "Collage," recorded for The Mod Squad soundtrack in 1999. The Deal sisters recruited new personnel to play several live shows in 2001, and returned to the studio with guitarist Richard Presley, bass player Mando Lopez and drummer Jose Medeles to record the third Breeders studio album "Title TK" with Steve Albini. The Breeders were also recruited, in early 2002, to perform in an episode of Buffy the Vampire Slayer. They were approached by the production staff, after they had been performing the show's theme, originally written by Nerf Herder, as a regular part of their concert set for a long time. The episode is entitled Him, and aired November 5th of 2002. In 2004, Warner Music Group announced plans to drop the Breeders from their label following low album sales of "Title TK." The decision came with Warner's plans to drop several other artists as well. The new album called "Mountain Battles" was released in the first half of 2008. The band lineup is the same as Title TK, minus Richard Presley.

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org
