events.summary: Vibrational Wellness: Find your frequency. You are invited to move from doing to being within the historic, industrial landscape of the Goldsmith Blocks in Old Town Portland. This soundscape is designed to settle the nervous system and deepen the breath, creating a space where sound acts as both guardian and guide. By allowing the external and internal noise to quiet, the mind is encouraged into a state of profound rest and presence. Through a bespoke collection of instruments and frequencies, we work to bypass the analytical mind—allowing the body to move into a state of recovery with more guidance than traditional meditation. This practice is an opportunity to reconnect with an experience that is both ancient and immutable, offering a grounded and tangible path to mindfulness. Held in a second-floor warehouse space defined by a wall of natural light, this space offers an elevated retreat from the busy streets below. Occasionally we hear the ambient hum of the city, and use those moments in collaboration with our intended sounds to further anchor us to the present. This gentle, accessible practice is for anyone seeking to reconnect with their inner stillness; no prior experience is needed to enjoy or benefit from this session. While most choose to lie still, you are welcome to engage in gentle yoga or stretching if that serves you—we just ask that you remain mindful of your neighbors' space and the shared quiet. All respectful beings are welcome. The Benefits Beyond the rest itself, we work with specific frequencies intended to: Lower stress and increase your sense of presence. Soothe emotional fatigue and help build resiliency. Quiet sensory overload and invite inner quiet. Lower cortisol to support better sleep quality. What to Bring for Comfort We will be on a hardwood floor in a warehouse setting, so please bring whatever you need to feel fully supported for the hour. The Padded Sanctuary: For your convenience, a limited number of "Padded Sanctuary" tickets are available. These include a pre-set premium mat, blanket, and pillows waiting for you upon arrival. The Essential Ticket: Please bring your own "nest"—a thick mat, blankets (it is easier to relax when you are warm), and pillows for your head or knees. You are welcome to bring a gravity chair if it makes you happy. Note: These are cleansing and charging sessions. Please feel free to bring water, crystals, tarot cards, or other small items you may want “bathed” in the resonance. Key Logistics Location: The Goldsmith Blocks, 2nd Floor, Old Town Portland. Universally accessible via elevator. Parking: Paid parking is available in the lot directly across the street, as well as metered street parking throughout the area. Please allow extra time to navigate the city and settle in. Timing: Doors open at 10:45 AM and the journey begins at 11:00 AM. Arriving early helps you maintain a shared sense of calm as we start promptly. Investment: I offer a tiered ticket structure to keep these sessions sustainable and accessible. Please choose the price point that feels authentic for your practice today. Certified member of the International Sound Therapy Association.
events.title: Vibrational Wellness: A Sound Bath Immersion Meditation

The Oregon Rail Heritage Center’s popular weekend train rides return May 23 through October 11, 2026, with departures every Saturday and Sunday behind historic diesel locomotive BNSF 3613. Perfect for families, visitors, and train lovers of all ages, these scenic excursions offer a unique way to experience Portland from the rails. Whether it’s your first train ride or a favorite family tradition, this classic Portland experience is one you won’t want to miss! When: Saturdays & Sundays, May 23 – October 11, 2026 Where: Oregon Rail Heritage Center, 2250 SE Water Ave., Portland, OR, 97214 Ticket Prices: • Adults (14+): $17 • Children (3–13): $12 • Seniors (65+) & Military: $15 • Family Pass: $50 (2 adults + 2 children) • Infants under 3 ride free on a lap Advance ticket purchase is recommended. events.summary: This summer, a multi-sensory art experience called Shifting Realities will take over Porsche Studio Portland for a creative journey produced by artists from Portland and across the country. The space turns into a living canvas where you don’t just observe the work, you become part of it. Across multiple interactive environments, you’ll see sound take physical form, design in real time using light and gesture, and step into spaces that respond to your movement, energy, and input. From large-scale visual installations to hands-on creative moments and a multisensory tasting experience, each part of the experience is designed to blur the line between artist and audience. Guests move through the experience in timed groups, progressing together through each space while still having room to explore and interact along the way. Running June 4 through August 31, Shifting Realities is a 100 minute limited-run installation that’s built for all ages and occasions. Tickets start at $39 ($41.34 incl. fees), with reduced pricing for kids and options for VIP, private, and group bookings.
events.title: Shifting Realities: A New Immersive Art Exhibition at Porsche Studio

events.summary: Renegade Opera announces two new works as part of the Artists in Conversation Festival, an annual program that explores the future of opera and the performing arts through the lens of diversity, equity, and inclusion. The 2026 Artists in Conversation Festival presents live performances of two concert works, We’re Still Here: A Love Song to Queer Composers* and *Duo Cantilena: An Exploration of Guitar and Voice Music. Each concert will be followed by a conversation with the performers and creators, an opportunity to learn, explore, and expand your understanding of what it means to tell stories through music for today’s audiences. We’re Still Here is a celebration of queer composers and queer love through the ages, featuring works from both modern and classical composers who loved or identified outside the bounds of traditional ideas. The program features local artists Madeleine Tran, Eulis Kay, and Claire Forstman and includes a diverse array of songs ranging from art song repertoire from Poulenc, Barber, Copland, and little-known queer female historical composers Ethyl Smyth and Adele Maddison, as well as modern selections from pop favorites like Brandi Carlisle and George Michael. Join us at Artist’s Repertory Theater at 7pm on August 29th and 1pm on August 30th for this sometimes poignant, sometimes hilarious program! Duo Cantilena is made up of husband and wife duo Joshua Bavaro, guitarist and Emily Evelyn Way, soprano. They perform art song repertoire for voice and classical guitar. With grace, poise, and fearless expressivity, they bring new life to repertoire written across the ages, and showcase song cycles rarely heard. The pair met while studying music at Manhattan School of Music and have performed together ever since. Their current program starts with Italian art songs from the early 1800’s and travels through Germany, Spain, and lands in contemporary English and American repertoire. The final set of the program, Confiding, was written by Joshua’s guitar teacher at MSM, a sweet return to the beginnings of where Duo Cantilena was originally formed. More information can be found on our website.
events.title: Renegade Opera's Artists in Conversation Festival 2026

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour

events.summary: The Weill & Brel Show: The Human Condition in Song "A tonic for our times... a call to action... and a reminder that we are not alone." "We all need to hear what you have to offer." History doesn't begin as history. It begins with ordinary people asking, What is happening to the world? And sometimes, more quietly, What is happening to me? Kurt Weill composed through the artistic brilliance of Weimar Germany, the rise of fascism, exile, World War II, and ultimately Broadway. Jacques Brel spent his childhood under the shadow of that war, then devoted his career to laying bare the human heart. Both understood that the greatest struggles are never only political. They are deeply human. What happens when fear begins to shape a society? What happens when it begins to shape us? The Weill & Brel Show: The Human Condition in Song is an intimate cabaret-style experience built around those questions. Through insightful narration, seamless translations, and a fourth wall that gradually disappears, audiences aren't simply watching songs from another era—they're invited to recognize themselves within them. You may know more of this music than you realize. The evening features Mack the Knife and Pirate Jenny from The Threepenny Opera, music from Weill's Broadway years, original Jacques Brel chansons including Ne Me Quitte Pas (If You Go Away), and selections made famous by the unconventional musical revue Jacques Brel Is Alive and Well and Living in Paris. The show grew from a one-hour preview at The Old Church that drew an extraordinary audience response and has since expanded into a fully realized two-hour experience. Audiences have called it "stunning," "an honor to be there," and "an extraordinary program... woven seamlessly together by narration and translation." One reviewer wrote, "Ne Me Quitte Pas absolutely broke my heart... When she dropped to her knees, I felt like I fell off a cliff." More than a portrait of two extraordinary composers, The Weill & Brel Show invites audiences to encounter artists who lived through extraordinary upheaval yet refused to surrender their humanity. Perhaps that's why these songs don't feel like history. They sound like your story, and mine. Experience the show in an intimate cabaret setting with bistro tables, a full bar, and light snacks. Performances Friday, August 28, 2026 • 7:00–9:00 p.m. Saturday, August 29, 2026 • 7:00–9:00 p.m. The Burlingame Space 8423 SW Terwilliger Blvd. Portland, OR 97219 There is more information at: TheWeillAndBrelShow.com

We’re Still Here is a celebration of queer composers and queer love through the ages, featuring works from both modern and classical composers who loved or identified outside the bounds of traditional ideas. The program features local artists Madeleine Tran, Eulis Kay, and Claire Forstman and includes a diverse array of songs ranging from art song repertoire from Poulenc, Barber, Copland, and little-known queer female historical composers Ethyl Smyth and Adele Maddison, as well as modern selections from pop favorites like Brandi Carlisle and George Michael. Join us at Artist’s Repertory Theater at 7pm on August 29th and 1pm on August 30th for this sometimes poignant, sometimes hilarious program! Duo Cantilena is made up of husband and wife duo Joshua Bavaro, guitarist and Emily Evelyn Way, soprano. They perform art song repertoire for voice and classical guitar. With grace, poise, and fearless expressivity, they bring new life to repertoire written across the ages, and showcase song cycles rarely heard. The pair met while studying music at Manhattan School of Music and have performed together ever since. Their current program starts with Italian art songs from the early 1800’s and travels through Germany, Spain, and lands in contemporary English and American repertoire. The final set of the program, Confiding, was written by Joshua’s guitar teacher at MSM, a sweet return to the beginnings of where Duo Cantilena was originally formed. More information can be found on our website.
events.title: Renegade Opera's Artists in Conversation Festival 2026

events.summary: Portland premiere of the new restoration! Part of the Hanabi Film Festival 2026. Limited festival passes available while supplies last. Doors open at 6:30 PM; film at 7:00 PM. An exuberant farce tinted with deep shades of melancholy and real violence, Shinji Sōmai’s under-seen gem is an ode to the dreams of youth against authority centering on three teens on an odyssey to rescue their kidnapped class bully from a gang of yakuza. En route they run afoul of some cops, befriend a motley former gangster, and experience the first seismic shocks of growing up. What carries them along is less the search for their classmate than the sheer momentum of being young and alive. Across the film, Sōmai constantly invents astonishing new ways to capture their movements, including a mythic opening shot, which—according to legend—required the use of three cranes. Adapted from a comic strip-like scenario by Leonard and Chieko Schrader, it’s a film of unparalleled freedom, and a testament to Somai’s ability to inject his work with life. Screened in Japanese with English subtitles. Director: Shinji Sōmai Year: 1983 Country: Japan Runtime: 118 minutes

events.summary: Medical experts play a crucial role in evaluating injuries that occur during assisted childbirth by carefully reviewing medical records, delivery notes, imaging scans, and the condition of both the mother and baby. They assess whether forceps, vacuum extraction, or other assisted delivery methods were used appropriately according to accepted medical standards. Specialists also examine the timing of interventions, fetal monitoring records, and whether alternative delivery options should have been considered. Their findings help determine if the injuries resulted from unavoidable complications or preventable medical negligence. In cases involving Traume from Instrumental Delivery, experts evaluate the extent of physical and neurological harm, the expected long-term impact, and the treatment or rehabilitation that may be required. They may consult with obstetricians, pediatric neurologists, radiologists, and rehabilitation professionals to provide an objective medical opinion. This expert evidence is often essential in establishing whether the standard of care fell below what would reasonably be expected. A detailed medical assessment can also help quantify the financial and personal impact of the injury, including ongoing healthcare needs and loss of quality of life. Families seeking answers often rely on experienced legal professionals to interpret these findings within the context of a compensation claim. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases, including those involving assisted childbirth injuries, and works closely with independent medical experts to build well-supported claims. By combining detailed medical evidence with legal expertise, the firm helps clients understand their rights and pursue fair compensation where negligence has contributed to avoidable birth injuries.
events.title: How do medical experts assess injuries caused by assisted childbirth?

events.summary: Instrumental delivery can be a necessary medical intervention during childbirth, but when forceps or a vacuum extractor are used incorrectly, mothers may suffer serious physical and emotional harm. Injuries such as severe perineal tears, pelvic floor damage, nerve injuries, excessive bleeding, or long-term pain can have lasting effects on daily life. If these injuries resulted from avoidable medical errors or substandard care, the affected mother may have grounds to pursue a compensation claim. Establishing negligence typically requires evidence that healthcare professionals failed to meet the accepted standard of care and that this directly caused the injury. Every case is unique, so medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the delivery are carefully evaluated. Claims can help recover compensation for medical expenses, rehabilitation, lost income, ongoing care, and pain and suffering. The physical and emotional Traume from Instrumental Delivery may also be considered when assessing the full impact of the injury on the mother's quality of life. Understanding your legal rights is an important first step toward seeking justice. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance to individuals who believe their injuries were caused by negligent medical treatment. Their experience in investigating childbirth-related negligence helps clients understand whether they have a valid claim and what legal options may be available. Seeking legal advice promptly can also help preserve important evidence and ensure claims are brought within the applicable time limits.
events.title: Maternal injuries during instrumental delivery lead to compensation claims?

events.summary: Proving a Surgical Negligence claim requires strong, well-documented evidence that demonstrates how a healthcare provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and caused avoidable harm. Medical records are often the foundation of the case, providing a detailed timeline of diagnosis, treatment, surgery, and follow-up care. Expert medical opinions are equally important because they help establish whether the surgeon's actions fell below the standard expected of a reasonably competent professional. Diagnostic scans, laboratory results, surgical notes, consent forms, and hospital records can further support the claim. Witness statements from medical professionals or others involved in the patient's care may also strengthen the evidence. It is essential to show not only that an error occurred but also that the mistake directly resulted in physical, emotional, or financial damage. Documentation of ongoing treatment, rehabilitation, lost income, and future medical needs can help demonstrate the full impact of the injury. Every case is unique, making a thorough investigation critical before legal proceedings begin. An experienced solicitor can identify the evidence needed, obtain independent expert reports, and build a compelling legal argument. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases and understands the detailed approach required to investigate Surgical Negligence claims. Their experience in reviewing medical evidence and working with independent experts helps clients present well-supported claims. By carefully gathering relevant documentation and establishing causation, they aim to protect the rights of individuals affected by avoidable surgical errors. Seeking legal guidance early can also help preserve important evidence and ensure procedural deadlines are met. A well-prepared case supported by credible evidence significantly improves the likelihood of achieving a fair outcome.
events.title: What evidence is required to prove a surgical negligence claim?

events.summary: When parents suspect that a birth injury could have been prevented, taking prompt and informed action is essential. The first step is to seek appropriate medical care for the child and ensure that all ongoing health concerns are properly documented. Parents should also request copies of medical records, including labour, delivery, and neonatal care notes, as these documents may help clarify what happened during childbirth. It is often beneficial to keep a detailed record of symptoms, treatments, and conversations with healthcare providers. In some situations, concerns may arise about Traume from Instrumental Delivery, particularly if forceps or a vacuum extractor were used during a difficult birth and the child later developed injuries. While not every complication is the result of negligence, a thorough legal review can determine whether accepted medical standards were followed. Understanding the cause of a birth injury can help families make informed decisions about their next steps. Experienced legal professionals can explain the claims process, the evidence required, and the applicable time limits without creating unnecessary stress for parents. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on medical negligence cases, including birth injury claims, and provides guidance to families seeking answers after a traumatic delivery. Most importantly, parents should remember that seeking legal advice is not only about pursuing compensation but also about obtaining accountability and securing support for their child's future care and long-term needs.

events.summary: Surgical negligence under Irish law occurs when a surgeon, hospital, or other healthcare professional fails to provide the standard of care that a reasonably competent medical practitioner would have delivered in similar circumstances, resulting in avoidable harm to a patient. This can include operating on the wrong site, causing preventable surgical injuries, failing to obtain informed consent, leaving surgical instruments inside the body, or providing inadequate post-operative care. Every case is assessed on its own facts, and proving Surgical Negligence generally requires evidence showing that the accepted standard of medical care was breached and that the breach directly caused the injury. Patients may experience additional medical treatment, prolonged recovery, financial losses, or long-term physical and emotional effects because of negligent surgical care. Irish law allows eligible patients to seek compensation where negligence can be established through appropriate medical and legal evidence. Understanding your legal rights early can make a significant difference in protecting your interests and preserving important evidence. Seeking advice from experienced legal professionals helps clarify whether the circumstances meet the legal threshold for Surgical Negligence. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on representing clients in complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance throughout the legal process with a clear understanding of Irish medical negligence law. Their experience in handling surgical negligence cases helps clients understand the evidence required, the claims process, and the potential outcomes. Whether the issue involves a surgical error, delayed treatment after surgery, or another avoidable complication, obtaining informed legal advice is an important first step toward pursuing justice and fair compensation.
events.title: What is considered surgical negligence under Irish law?

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Converge 45 Triennial: Here, To you, Now Dates: August 27–30, 2026 \(Opening Weekend\); programming continues through Fall 2026 Locations: 16 partner venues across Portland, Oregon Converge 45 is Portland’s citywide contemporary art triennial, bringing together 28 local and international artists across 16 venues throughout the city. Curated by Lumi Tan, the 2026 edition—Here, To you, Now—features 17 brand-new art commissions inspired by the writings of iconic Portland author Ursula K. Le Guin, centering on themes of impermanence, storytelling, and the unique, temporary communities that form around art. Visitors can explore a wide array of mediums—including video, animation, dance, visual arts, and interactive installations—hosted at galleries, colleges, public spaces, and cultural hubs across the region, such as PICA, PNCA, Oregon Contemporary, Reser Center for the Arts, and Portland International Airport. Opening weekend \(August 27–30\) kicks off the season with citywide receptions, live performances, film screenings, and artist talks. Visit converge45.org for more info.

events.summary: Renegade Opera announces two new works as part of the Artists in Conversation Festival, an annual program that explores the future of opera and the performing arts through the lens of diversity, equity, and inclusion. The 2026 Artists in Conversation Festival presents live performances of two concert works, We’re Still Here: A Love Song to Queer Composers* and *Duo Cantilena: An Exploration of Guitar and Voice Music. Each concert will be followed by a conversation with the performers and creators, an opportunity to learn, explore, and expand your understanding of what it means to tell stories through music for today’s audiences. We’re Still Here is a celebration of queer composers and queer love through the ages, featuring works from both modern and classical composers who loved or identified outside the bounds of traditional ideas. The program features local artists Madeleine Tran, Eulis Kay, and Claire Forstman and includes a diverse array of songs ranging from art song repertoire from Poulenc, Barber, Copland, and little-known queer female historical composers Ethyl Smyth and Adele Maddison, as well as modern selections from pop favorites like Brandi Carlisle and George Michael. Join us at Artist’s Repertory Theater at 7pm on August 29th and 1pm on August 30th for this sometimes poignant, sometimes hilarious program! Duo Cantilena is made up of husband and wife duo Joshua Bavaro, guitarist and Emily Evelyn Way, soprano. They perform art song repertoire for voice and classical guitar. With grace, poise, and fearless expressivity, they bring new life to repertoire written across the ages, and showcase song cycles rarely heard. The pair met while studying music at Manhattan School of Music and have performed together ever since. Their current program starts with Italian art songs from the early 1800’s and travels through Germany, Spain, and lands in contemporary English and American repertoire. The final set of the program, Confiding, was written by Joshua’s guitar teacher at MSM, a sweet return to the beginnings of where Duo Cantilena was originally formed. More information can be found on our website.
events.title: Renegade Opera's Artists in Conversation Festival 2026

events.summary: Climb aboard for a memorable rail adventure through the heart of Portland! The Oregon Rail Heritage Center’s popular weekend train rides return May 23 through October 11, 2026, with departures every Saturday and Sunday behind historic diesel locomotive BNSF 3613. Perfect for families, visitors, and train lovers of all ages, these scenic excursions offer a unique way to experience Portland from the rails. Passengers can ride in an open-air car or relax in a vintage air-conditioned coach while taking in views of Portland’s skyline, the riverfront, local wildlife, and the timeless charm of Oaks Park. Your ticket also includes admission to the Oregon Rail Heritage Center, where guests can explore Portland’s rich rail history and see historic locomotives up close. Whether it’s your first train ride or a favorite family tradition, this classic Portland experience is one you won’t want to miss! When: Saturdays & Sundays, May 23 – October 11, 2026 Where: Oregon Rail Heritage Center, 2250 SE Water Ave., Portland, OR, 97214 Ticket Prices: • Adults (14+): $17 • Children (3–13): $12 • Seniors (65+) & Military: $15 • Family Pass: $50 (2 adults + 2 children) • Infants under 3 ride free on a lap Advance ticket purchase is recommended. Service charges apply. Please arrive at least 20 minutes before departure for check-in and boarding.

events.summary: This summer, a multi-sensory art experience called Shifting Realities will take over Porsche Studio Portland for a creative journey produced by artists from Portland and across the country. The space turns into a living canvas where you don’t just observe the work, you become part of it. Across multiple interactive environments, you’ll see sound take physical form, design in real time using light and gesture, and step into spaces that respond to your movement, energy, and input. From large-scale visual installations to hands-on creative moments and a multisensory tasting experience, each part of the experience is designed to blur the line between artist and audience. Guests move through the experience in timed groups, progressing together through each space while still having room to explore and interact along the way. Running June 4 through August 31, Shifting Realities is a 100 minute limited-run installation that’s built for all ages and occasions. Tickets start at $39 ($41.34 incl. fees), with reduced pricing for kids and options for VIP, private, and group bookings.
events.title: Shifting Realities: A New Immersive Art Exhibition at Porsche Studio

events.summary: The Hatchery is a revolutionary annual new works festival that supports the creation of music and movement-centered theater by providing time, space, and resources for theater-makers to realize their artistic goals. Following two weeks of intensive new work development in the studio, two production teams will welcome the public into their theater-making process with two days of work-in-progress performances. This year’s projects include Undertow, a new musical adapted from the award-winning queer, Peruvian film Contracorriente, and The Cannery Project, an educational play about the legacy of an Alaskan salmon cannery told through historical documentation, factory-inspired movement, and song. Audiences will experience each full-length project as a semi-staged work-in-progress performance. Sliding-scale/pay-what-you-will tickets are available. All events on Saturday, August 29, are ASL-Interpreted. Duo Cantilena is made up of husband and wife duo Joshua Bavaro, guitarist and Emily Evelyn Way, soprano. They perform art song repertoire for voice and classical guitar. With grace, poise, and fearless expressivity, they bring new life to repertoire written across the ages, and showcase song cycles rarely heard. The pair met while studying music at Manhattan School of Music and have performed together ever since. Their current program starts with Italian art songs from the early 1800’s and travels through Germany, Spain, and lands in contemporary English and American repertoire. The final set of the program, Confiding, was written by Joshua’s guitar teacher at MSM, a sweet return to the beginnings of where Duo Cantilena was originally formed. More information can be found on our website.

events.summary: DJ Anjali and The Incredible Kid’s Holi Summer Fest A Celebration of Color McMenamins Grand Lodge 3505 Pacific Ave, Forest Grove, Ore. 97116 Sunday, August 30th (Note this is postponed from June 28th due to rain!) 3:30-7:30PM All-Ages Tickets are 28.10 dollars in advance. https://www.etix.com/ticket/p/34994316/holi-summer-festa-celebration-of-color-forest-grove-mcmenamins-grand-lodge HOLI HAI! After four sold-out Holi Festivals Anjali & The Kid bring their color throw experience to Forest Grove for their biggest Holi yet featuring all organic colors handmade by farmers and tribal communities in India. A Bollywood and Bhangra dance party in the grass with Anjali’s Gulabi Gang dance troupe and the PDX Bhangra troupe. Color throws at 4:30, 5:30 & 6:30PM. Note that the actual date of Holi occurs in March, but in the Pacific Northwest celebrations of the festival are often pushed back as far as June (or if June is rained out, August!) to take advantage of better weather and dancing in the grass. This event features only-organic powder, direct from India, made from flowers, seeds and vegetables (like rose, spinach, marigold and turmeric.) Each paid entrance includes a packet of colors and a portion of the festival proceeds will benefit farmers in India. Other Holi festivals typically feature industrial dyes containing carcinogens; this event is committed to returning to plant-based powder which honors our connection to the earth. Everyone is welcome at this all-ages event. Expect to get messy as Holi is celebrated by throwing bright colored powder on each other. Wearing white or old clothes is recommended. No outside colors are allowed. Each ticket holder will receive one packet of complimentary powder. All sales final, no refunds or exchange Event details https://grandlodgeconcerts.com/event/holi-summer-fest Anjali DJed her first Holi in the Portland metro area in 2002 and then a long series of Holi events over the decades including many years in the Seattle area with over 10,000 people in attendance. From the beginning Anjali saw how other promoters threw their events and wanted to do something different for her own festival. She wanted a Holi festival dedicated to the agricultural roots with a dance floor on the land, which necessitated a later start date in the PNW than the traditional date in March, to avoid trashing wet, soggy land that isn’t ready to have 1000s of people dancing on it. She envisioned a festival focused on organic powders hand-crafted in India and not synthetic neurotoxic factory products which often contain hazardous chemicals and heavy metals, like lead and mercury. In 2022 Anjali first partnered with Topaz Farm to throw four years of sold-out Holi festivals with 2,000 yearly in attendance and now in 2026 Anjali moves the party to McMenamin’s Grand Lodge in Forest Grove for an even larger celebration.

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. events.summary: In the latest novel from Claire Vaye Watkins, "our most significant rising writer of the American West" \(Vulture\), an unfettered heroine searches for a new way to love, and live, in a deeply uncertain world. The first time Rose fell for Miles, she was a college kid, all too eager to be swept into his sexy orbit; little wonder the relationship crashed and burned. When Miles comes back into her life two decades later, he finds a different Rose. Not only has she moved back to her beloved desert, on a homestead she’s dubbed Nothingness Flats, but she’s chosen to live “on the other side of the portal,” with an intentionality that’s brought her hard-won peace and freedom. She’s navigating single parenthood, and she’s found a community out at Yellow Pine, where a group of spirited misfits have mounted a stand against the corporatization of solar power. Is it worth jeopardizing all this for another chance with Miles? And yet the universe seems to be beckoning her, not only back to him but possibly toward another child. What shape might her future take, on this side of the portal? As furious, funny, searching, and searingly original as ever, in Yellow Pine \(Riverhead\) Watkins blazes a trail toward a radically reimagined vision of a good life in a precarious age. Watkins will be joined in conversation by Gabriel Urza, author of The Silver State. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/claire-vaye-watkins-9798217045020
events.title: Powell's Presents: Claire Vaye Watkins in Conversation With Gabriel Urza

From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Featuring artwork by Gordon Campbell, Angela Holm, Tie Li, Emily Krupp-Pederson, Karen Shawcross Five artists reflect on the beauty and emotional resonance of Pacific Northwest landscapes. Spanning a variety of mediums, the exhibition brings together works in which artists trace the many ways the place they call home can be seen, experienced, and remembered. Stroll through the gallery, meet the artists, and enjoy art activities and refreshments. From 6 - 7 pm, photographer Angela Holm will give an interactive artist talk, where guests can examine a selection of photographs alongside the cameras used to create them and make their own guesses about which camera made each image. Angela will then reveal the pairings while sharing why she chose each camera, how its unique qualities shaped the resulting photograph, and what can happen when an artist changes not only the tool, but the way they see. Part artist talk, part visual investigation, the presentation invites guests to look more closely, question their assumptions, and discover how process can transform the familiar into something unexpected.

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season

events.summary: As John Gardner remarks in The Art of Fiction, “What the beginning writer ordinarily wants is a set of rules on what to do and what not to do in writing fiction.” And while general rules exist, Gardner observes that such “supposed aesthetic absolutes prove relative under pressure. They’re laws, but they slip,” he says. Indeed, many of the stories that touch us—those whose impact lingers for months, if not years, after we turn the final page—are constructed with these general rules of craft in mind. Although this course will predominantly take the form of a workshop, it will also provide insights into the craft of writing by drawing upon principles from The Art of Fiction, essays on literary craft, and published short stories. By exploring the “absolutes” that govern fiction and creative nonfiction, students will equip themselves to bend if not break these rules in service of the stories they seek to tell. Designed for beginner and advanced writers, this course meets for ten sessions total. Students will have the opportunity to share two pieces \(up to 25 pages each\) and receive constructive feedback in a thoughtfully facilitated, supportive atmosphere. Although not required, students may wish to obtain a copy of Gardner’s Art of Fiction. All other readings to be provided. Access Program We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available. Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions. Liaison position Every in-person class and seminar at Literary Arts has one liaison position. Liaisons perform specific duties for each class meeting. If you are a liaison for a class or seminar, the full amount of your tuition is covered by Literary Arts. Apply here for the liaison position.

events.summary: The New York Times bestselling author of The Immortalists returns with an intimate yet epic love story — and a sweeping odyssey of scientific discovery. Under Story \(G. P. Putnam’s Sons\) invites us to consider the promise of this life, what might lie beyond it, and how far we would go for more time with the people we love, cementing Chloe Benjamin’s place among our best, and most lasting, storytellers. “We wake up to tomorrow, never yesterday.” At the edge of the world, biologist Laurel Salter is hiding from everything she’s ever known. For ten hours a day, six days per week, she works as a dishwasher at McMurdo Station, an isolated research base in Antarctica. She tells no one that before she arrived, she was a renowned young scientist with a promising career and a family. But even in this remote outpost, Laurel can’t escape her past. When a strange light appears across the ice — and draws a group of physicists to McMurdo — her former husband, Eli, won't be far behind. Laurel is captivated by the Arc: its surreal glow; the way it seems almost alive. And though Eli is reluctant to test her wildest theory, Laurel is convinced that the Arc leads down a rabbit hole and into a world they can barely imagine. Can she persuade him to risk everything to fix the burden that hangs between them — to turn back the clock and live their story a second time? A breathless page-turner and a love letter to our planet, Under Story grapples with the great questions of our time: human hubris, the precarity of the natural world, and the mysterious webs of consciousness that bind us. A modern epic of science and soul, of bravery and redemption, it offers a vision of the future that demands we reckon with what we owe to one another, and to the earth itself. Benjamin will be joined in conversation by Lydia Kiesling, author of Mobility. Please note: This is a ticketed event. Tickets include admission, as well as one hardcover copy of Under Story. events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org

events.summary: This former Southern Pacific Railroad station, fondly called the Old Train Station \(OTS\), is home to Friends of Historic Forest Grove. The Old Train Station now serves as a museum highlighting about 150 years of local history, from photographs and maps to clothing and furniture. It also houses an historic library and research center. Built in 1913, the station handled passenger and light freight service into 1929. After that only light freight came through. Burlingham and Sons purchased the building as office space for their seed company. Unfortunately, over the years this building has gone through some internal and external changes but some of the original station remains and can easy be found. Woodfold acquired the building from Burlingham and has graciously allowed Friends to use the building since 2008. Please stop by and see what we have to offer. Check website to confirm open hours

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season

events.summary: Roni Size’s whole life has been about building something new from whatever was around him. From Bristol youthclub parties, through the white heat of rave and the founding moments of jungle and drum’n’bass, to transforming underground electronic music into something that could be played by a live band on the biggest arena and festival stages, he has at each stage created completely afresh - not just a sound or style but an entire methodology of how music can be made. And each time, that new creation has reflected his heritage, his surroundings and the precise moment in which he’s operating. 20-years ago, The Mercury Prize win for his ‘New Forms’ album brought D’n’B to the forefront of dance-music news, making even the rest of the industry – where reactions had up until that point been bemused – sit up and pay attention. For several years thereafter Roni and team were on top of the world, succeeding as solo artists as well as a collective, maintaining underground credibility yet receiving Brit awards and even collaborating with some of the biggest names in hip hop. 2016 was a vintage year for Roni. Live shows included Ram Records’ NYE show at O2 Academy Brixton, a headline show at the BBC 6 Music festival and a summer festival season that began at Love Saves the Day with a curated Full Cycle Stage Takeover for Arcadia Afterburner and included Secret Garden Party, Evolution, Glastonbury, Blissfields, NASS, EDC, Dour, Boomtown, Frequency, Lowlands, Creamfields, SW4, Outlook, and many more. Roni relaunched Full Cycle Records with fellow co-founder, DJ Krust, with the releases drawing praise from The Wire, Dummy, UKF, Mista Jam, 6 Music, Gilles Peterson, Radio 1, 1Xtra, DJ Mag and beyond. It was in 2017, as we fully appreciated the legacy that Roni has created for drum’n’bass, that the next chapter began. Roni toured his groundbreaking new audio visual live show, a combined live instrument and hardware show that features state of the art production and 3D effect projection mapping celebrating 20 years of New Forms. Roni took the groundbreaking live show on the road to festivals in the UK and Europe as well as on extensive tours of the US, New Zealand and Australia with no let up as he also DJ’ed at the very best clubs and festivals throughout the globe. The anniversary re-release of New Forms (on Universal and featuring the live set together with brand new remixes, edits and tracks) garnered huge support across digital and print media as well as on radio. With premieres from MixMag and Tsugi, rave reviews and coverage by NME, Fact, DJ Mag, Clash and many others along with multiple plays on BBC Radio 1 and BBC Radio 1 Xtra, Roni cemented his position at the top of the game. The man from Bristol showed no signs of slowing down, as he took to the road with UK and European live tours in 2018 and continued to travel to all corners of the globe to play clubs and festivals including Dirtybird Campout, Noisily, Blue Dot, Output, Creamfields and SW4. Roni finished 2018 with a remix for rising star Paris Green on Get Physical and played shows in Europe, the US, Australia, Asia and Brazil as well as appearing on guest spots across BBC Radio and continuing to contribute to charity projects and support the grass roots scene in his home city of Bristol. 2019 continued on a high. Roni worked on huge collab track “Calling” with Rag n Bone Man, which was selected as the “sound of summer” by Sky Sports and broadcast repeatedly across their channels. Roni appeared on BBC TV as well as regularly on radio and had his music chosen by Virgil Abloh to curate the designer’s Off White runway shows. Meanwhile, Roni played the likes of Printworks, Tomorrowland, Eastern Electrics, Fabric, Untold Festival and countless others. Roni ended 2019 as the face of highly-respected music tech brands Waves and Krotos, recognised for his contribution to the industry and his knowledge and skill as a producer.
events.title: Roni Size

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists
