events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/Buress26 On Sale Friday, July 10 at 10am PT ---------------------------------------- From within the bustling heart of the Windy City, a comedian named Hannibal Buress embarked upon his journey. The year was 2002, the location, the Big Muddy Room at Southern Illinois University. Guided by the wisdom of his friend Chidi and sharpened in the fires of Tony Trimm's "Sunday School sessions," young Buress was prepared to take the comedy world by storm. In 2006, he emerged from the shadows, performing at Montreal's 'Just for Laughs' New Faces, an event that led to his first international appearance on "Late Night with Jörgen Raymann" in Holland. From that moment, he continued to grow, creating a series of successful stand-up specials including "Animal Furnace," "Live From Chicago," "Hannibal Takes Edinburgh," "Comedy Camisado," and "Miami Nights". Fate intervened in 2009, when a last-minute booking on "Late Night with Jimmy Fallon" led to a meeting with Seth Meyers. This encounter gave him the opportunity to write for the legendary show "Saturday Night Live." It was there, my young turtles, where Buress had one sketch air – a moment he credits to the creativity of his cousin Percy. He cherishes the memory of watching Rihanna uttering his lines in the "Shy Ronnie" sketch. After a season there, he moved to "30 Rock," filling the space left vacant by the departure of Donald Glover. In the realm of film, Buress has proven his versatility, showcasing his talents in "Neighbors," "Neighbors 2," "Baywatch," "Daddy's Home," "Spiderman: Homecoming," "Spiderman: Far From Home," and "Tag." He also provided a memorable performance as Lincoln the dentist on "Broad City" and lent his voice to animations like "The Secret Life of Pets" and "The Angry Birds Movie." From 2009 to 2017, Buress held court at the "Comedy at the Knitting Factory," his charm and wit making an indelible mark on late-night television, featuring on shows such as "David Letterman," "Conan," "Stephen Colbert," and "The Daily Show with Trevor Noah." In 2022, he underwent a transformation, shedding his skin to become Eshu Tune in the world of music. His rhythmic anthems like "Veneers remix" with Danny Brown and Paul Wall, the lively bowling song "1-3 Pocket," and the meticulously crafted "I Lift Weights" echo through the streets. This endeavor was made possible through collaborations with creative minds like Kiefer, Tru, Eshu Tune, Wahsabi Papi, Kenny Segal, Eryn Allen Kane, and Haile Supreme. Through these transformations, Hannibal Buress remains a true warrior in the world of entertainment.
events.title: Hannibal Buress

Watch as two 16mm programming teams fire up their projectors and trade cinematic jabs back and forth by screening selections from the world-famous DENNIS NYBACK 16mm film archive! No one knows what will be screened next – cartoons, music, educational films, documentary shorts and weird advertisements run amok! There are no rules, no prisoners, and no show is the same! A one-of-a-kind film free-for-all that will amuse, confuse and contuse your cinematic soul! events.summary: Fourteen albums, two Grammy nominations, nearly a dozen major awards and more than four decades into a career like no other, Sonny Landreth is an artist who's found a different way to play guitar and then some. Music journalists have called the singer/songwriter/bandleader/slide guitar virtuoso everything from "an innovator on the order of Eddie Van Halen" \(All About Jazz\) to "one of the finest guitarists America has ever produced" \(Rock & Blues Muse\), while artists including John Hiatt, Mark Knopfler, Bonnie Raitt and Eric Clapton -who's famously said, "Sonny Landreth is probably the most underestimated musician on the planet, and also one of the most advanced" -consider him an invaluable colleague, collaborator and bonafide guitar hero. For the Lafayette, LA native, it's a journey of remarkable musicianship that began with his first guitar at age 12. By his 20's he was sitting in with local Creole and Cajun musicians and would soon become the first white member of Clifton Chenier's legendary Red Hot Louisiana Band. "Being raised in a community where music is such a huge part of the culture," Landreth explains, "loving Robert Johnson and Duane Allman as much as Mozart, I just absorbed every one of those influences and somehow crystallized it into my own style." Through it all, Landreth has discovered his music being embraced by fans of blues, rock, jazz, zydeco, country, Americana, world music and more. "Not being pinned down to any one genre can be a blessing and a curse," he laughs. "But I was always comfortable playing different styles because slide guitar can speak to any audience." And as anyone who's witnessed him as the opening performer for an unprecedented seven of Eric Clapton's Crossroads Guitar Festivals can attest, Landreth's slide wizardry is a consistent highlight of the world's most famous six-string summit. For Landreth, the future is an open road with the top down and the radio turned up. He's currently recording a new album and maintaining a busy touring schedule. But for a one-of-a-kind artist who continues to defy categorization, what keeps him going/growing as an ever innovative yet always down-to-earth performer? "I still believe that music can possess the same magic that we all felt when we were kids," Landreth says. "You want it to feel personal and be inspiring. Whenever my music communicates or resonates with people, it's a great affirmation." Minors ok when accompanied by a parent or guardian. Review our venue FAQ here ALL SALES ARE FINAL. This can include operating on the wrong site, causing preventable surgical injuries, failing to obtain informed consent, leaving surgical instruments inside the body, or providing inadequate post-operative care. Every case is assessed on its own facts, and proving Surgical Negligence generally requires evidence showing that the accepted standard of medical care was breached and that the breach directly caused the injury. Patients may experience additional medical treatment, prolonged recovery, financial losses, or long-term physical and emotional effects because of negligent surgical care. Irish law allows eligible patients to seek compensation where negligence can be established through appropriate medical and legal evidence. Understanding your legal rights early can make a significant difference in protecting your interests and preserving important evidence. events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Raised in England, Hynes started out as a teenage punk in the UK band Test Icicles before releasing two orchestral acoustic pop records as Lightspeed Champion. In 2011, he released Coastal Grooves, the first of four solo albums under themonikerBlood Orange. His album, Freetown Sound, was released to critical acclaim in 2016, and saw Hynes defined as one of the foremost musical voices of his time, receiving comparisons to the likes of Kendrick Lamar and D'Angelo for his own searing and soothing personal document of life as a black man in America. He has collaborated with Solange, Skepta, FKA twigs, Carly Rae Jepsen, A$AP Rocky, Charlotte Gainsbourg, Blondie, and many other artists, and was recently one of four artists invited to the Kennedy Center to perform alongside Philip Glass. In addition to his production work, he scored the film Palo Alto, directed by Gia Coppola. Negro Swan was written and produced by Hynes. Says Hynes: "My newest album is an exploration into my own and many types of black depression, an honest look at the corners of black existence, and the ongoing anxieties of queer/people of color. A reach back into childhood and modern traumas, and the things we do to get through it all. The underlying thread through each piece on the album is the idea of HOPE, and the lights we can try to turn on within ourselves with a hopefully positive outcome of helping others out of their darkness

THE EXPERIENCE: A Portland ENCORE screening of the 1926 Japanese Avant-Garde Experimental Film A PAGE OF MADNESS \(KURRUTTA ICHIPEIGI\) Directed by Teinosuke Kinugasa featuring a special live soundtrack performed by QUASI and SOFT RUMBLE \(Kathy Foster & Rachel Blumberg\). ON SCREEN: A Page of Madness 1926. Directed by Teinosuke Kinugasa. Runtime: 73 minutes. Lostfor 45 years until it was rediscovered by Kinugasa in his storehouse in 1971, the film is the product of anavant-gardegroup of artists in Japan known as the Shinkankakuha \(or School of New Perceptions\) who tried to overcomenaturalistic representation. The film is set in a mental institution in contemporary Japan and revolves around a man who takes a janitorial job at the institution after his wife is taken in as a patient there. Eventually, the janitor himself begins to slip into a fantasy world in his own mind, while the pain and suffering continue around him. Using superimpositions, rapid and insistent visual patterns, fantasy sequences, and the visual flamboyance of actors impersonating mad people, A Page of Madness builds an atmosphere of astonishing intensity. ON STAGE: QUASI \(Performers\) - Quasi was formed in 1993 by Janet Weiss and Sam Coomes, in Portland Oregon. Since then, the band has toured the world \(more or less\) however many times, and released a number of well-regarded albums on several of the most respected American indie labels, including Up, Touch and Go, Kill Rock Stars, and Sub Pop, and internationally with longtime comrades Domino Records. Concurrently, JW was a longtime member of Sleater-Kinney, as well as recording and/or touring with Courtney Barnett and Kurt Vile, Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks, Bright Eyes, the Shins, Elliott Smith, the Go-Betweens, and others, and is currently also a member of Portland band Slang. SC has worked with Elliott Smith, Built to Spill, Jandek, the Go-Betweens, and others, and has toured and recorded as a solo artist. He is also currently a member of Jon Spencer and the HITmakers. Trivia!: Both Janet and Sam are two-time members of the Oregon Music Hall of Fame - JW for Quasi and Sleater-Kinney, and SC for Quasi and Heatmiser. Soft Rumble \(Performers\) - An exciting collaboration between two of Portland's most prolific musicians: Kathy Foster of Roseblood, Thermals, All Girl Summer Fun Band, Wooly Mountain, Hurry Up and Slang. And Rachel Blumberg of Field Drums, Arch Cape, M. Ward, The Decemberists and Michael Hurley. AUD

events.summary: What does it mean to lead, to worship, or to seek perfection — especially when the mirror keeps changing shape? In Take Me to Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown, Corean-born, Pacific Northwest–based performance artist Monel Chang (aka Moldy Melon) dives headfirst into a kaleidoscopic exploration of beauty, power, and the absurd rituals of becoming. Part pansori opera, part clown confession, part K-beauty séance, this solo performance unfolds like a fever dream across three acts. We meet a traditional pansori singer, steeped in ancient song and wonder; a K-beauty devotee, consumed by an altar of serums, snails, and sheet masks; and a self-proclaimed dictator, leading a birthday party for themself with military precision and toddler rage. Each character teeters between the sacred and the ridiculous, revealing how rituals of transformation — whether spiritual, aesthetic, or political — can both liberate and imprison us. Through meticulous physicality, voice, and gesture, Chang conjures a world where skincare becomes salvation, laughter becomes resistance, and a dictator’s parade dissolves into a child’s tantrum. With cues of light, sound, and scent, the stage transforms into a surreal landscape of shifting identities — from vanity table to battlefield, from face mask to flag. At once hilarious and haunting, The Seoul of a Clown interrogates the myth of perfection — in beauty, in heritage, and in leadership — while celebrating the messy, clownish heart that beats beneath it all. Drawing from Korean folk traditions, contemporary clowning, and the heightened absurdity of global pop culture, Chang builds a world where the search for “flawless skin” mirrors the search for self, and where even dictators might cry under their makeup. The result is a sensorial and spiritual satire — a ritual of laughter, longing, and self-recognition. Whether you leave glowing, weeping, or simply moisturized, Take Me to Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown promises an unforgettable night at the edge of comedy and catharsis.
events.title: Take Me To Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown

Since releasing their first EP in 2018, the band have grown into regional favorites in the Pacific Northwest – amassing millions of streams while playing for big room audiences and supporting globally recognized acts like Franz Ferdinand, Young the Giant, and more. Drawing from strange, cult-leaning texts uncovered during a cross-country field-recording journey, the band has built a groove-driven, secular spiritual world rooted in communal soul and 1970s swagger. Their newest single, “Malibu by Midnight,” arrives as a recovered artifact rather than a conventional single. The song is a version of a composition the band “found,” preserved alongside fragments of mysterious text with no known origin. Recorded with restraint and warmth, it channels West Coast AM Gold, stacked harmonies, and late-night Laurel Canyon haze. Since their 2023 full-length Kicked Out of the Garden, which spent months on the NACC 200 and appeared on NPR’s Live Wire Radio, Family Worship Center has toured nationally, continued work on a new record, and performed as the live backing band for cult legend Donnie Emerson. Known for their ecstatic live shows featuring horns, harmonies, and piano-driven gospel soul, the band has been praised by KEXP as “truly the best live band I have seen in years.”

events.summary: 7pm doors, 8pm show All ages welcome Madison Ryann Ward Faith-based singer/songwriter Madison Ryann Ward writes warmhearted songs that mix mature pop and contemporary R&B with accents of gospel, blues, and folk. Previously signed to Rick Rubin's American Recordings, for which she cut the secular Beyond Me EP \(2019\), she has established herself as an independent artist with her own Zelda House Records, issuing a slew of singles before making her full-length debut with A New Thing \(2023\), a bright showcase for her commanding and understated voice. Ward grew up in her native Oklahoma hearing a wide range of music. Her mother played piano in church, and she soaked up blues and soul classics while working in her teens at her father's restaurant. A year-round athletic star in high school, Ward excelled in volleyball at Oklahoma University with plans of going pro. Her path changed after an informal cafeteria recording of her singing Aretha Franklin's "Chain of Fools" went viral. This encouraged Ward to build an online following with regular uploads of covers, and she eventually devoted herself to developing her voice and budding songwriting talent, leading to a deal with producer Rick Rubin and his American Recordings label. After she made her commercial debut with the Rex Rideout collaboration "Mirror" in 2018, Ward continued the next year with Beyond Me, a four-track EP featuring the equally lean and soulful ballad "BRKN." Ward then went independent, and from 2020 through 2022 progressed with singles such as "Higher," "Player," "Love&Adoration," and "Anchor." In 2023, she delivered A New Thing, an album over an hour in length with a few of the preceding singles placed throughout the sequence. ~ Andy Kellman, Rovi

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: When parents suspect that a birth injury could have been prevented, taking prompt and informed action is essential. Parents should also request copies of medical records, including labour, delivery, and neonatal care notes, as these documents may help clarify what happened during childbirth. It is often beneficial to keep a detailed record of symptoms, treatments, and conversations with healthcare providers. In some situations, concerns may arise about Traume from Instrumental Delivery, particularly if forceps or a vacuum extractor were used during a difficult birth and the child later developed injuries. While not every complication is the result of negligence, a thorough legal review can determine whether accepted medical standards were followed. Understanding the cause of a birth injury can help families make informed decisions about their next steps. Experienced legal professionals can explain the claims process, the evidence required, and the applicable time limits without creating unnecessary stress for parents. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on medical negligence cases, including birth injury claims, and provides guidance to families seeking answers after a traumatic delivery. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters can help parents understand whether avoidable errors may have contributed to their child's injuries. Taking early action also helps preserve important evidence and protects a family's legal rights. Most importantly, parents should remember that seeking legal advice is not only about pursuing compensation but also about obtaining accountability and securing support for their child's future care and long-term needs.

events.summary: Proving a Surgical Negligence claim requires strong, well-documented evidence that demonstrates how a healthcare provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and caused avoidable harm. Medical records are often the foundation of the case, providing a detailed timeline of diagnosis, treatment, surgery, and follow-up care. Expert medical opinions are equally important because they help establish whether the surgeon's actions fell below the standard expected of a reasonably competent professional. Diagnostic scans, laboratory results, surgical notes, consent forms, and hospital records can further support the claim. Witness statements from medical professionals or others involved in the patient's care may also strengthen the evidence. It is essential to show not only that an error occurred but also that the mistake directly resulted in physical, emotional, or financial damage. Documentation of ongoing treatment, rehabilitation, lost income, and future medical needs can help demonstrate the full impact of the injury. Every case is unique, making a thorough investigation critical before legal proceedings begin. An experienced solicitor can identify the evidence needed, obtain independent expert reports, and build a compelling legal argument. By carefully gathering relevant documentation and establishing causation, they aim to protect the rights of individuals affected by avoidable surgical errors. Seeking legal guidance early can also help preserve important evidence and ensure procedural deadlines are met. A well-prepared case supported by credible evidence significantly improves the likelihood of achieving a fair outcome.

events.summary: Medical experts play a crucial role in evaluating injuries that occur during assisted childbirth by carefully reviewing medical records, delivery notes, imaging scans, and the condition of both the mother and baby. They assess whether forceps, vacuum extraction, or other assisted delivery methods were used appropriately according to accepted medical standards. Specialists also examine the timing of interventions, fetal monitoring records, and whether alternative delivery options should have been considered. This expert evidence is often essential in establishing whether the standard of care fell below what would reasonably be expected. A detailed medical assessment can also help quantify the financial and personal impact of the injury, including ongoing healthcare needs and loss of quality of life. Families seeking answers often rely on experienced legal professionals to interpret these findings within the context of a compensation claim. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases, including those involving assisted childbirth injuries, and works closely with independent medical experts to build well-supported claims. events.summary: Surgical negligence under Irish law occurs when a surgeon, hospital, or other healthcare professional fails to provide the standard of care that a reasonably competent medical practitioner would have delivered in similar circumstances, resulting in avoidable harm to a patient. This can include operating on the wrong site, causing preventable surgical injuries, failing to obtain informed consent, leaving surgical instruments inside the body, or providing inadequate post-operative care. Every case is assessed on its own facts, and proving Surgical Negligence generally requires evidence showing that the accepted standard of medical care was breached and that the breach directly caused the injury. Patients may experience additional medical treatment, prolonged recovery, financial losses, or long-term physical and emotional effects because of negligent surgical care. Irish law allows eligible patients to seek compensation where negligence can be established through appropriate medical and legal evidence. Understanding your legal rights early can make a significant difference in protecting your interests and preserving important evidence. Seeking advice from experienced legal professionals helps clarify whether the circumstances meet the legal threshold for Surgical Negligence. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on representing clients in complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance throughout the legal process with a clear understanding of Irish medical negligence law. Their experience in handling surgical negligence cases helps clients understand the evidence required, the claims process, and the potential outcomes. Whether the issue involves a surgical error, delayed treatment after surgery, or another avoidable complication, obtaining informed legal advice is an important first step toward pursuing justice and fair compensation.
events.title: What is considered surgical negligence under Irish law?

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org
events.title: Bronze, Wood, and Clay Contemporary Sculpture Exhibitions at MAC

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: We ACCEPT the following \(Must be CLEAN, DRY, and WHITE\):Polystyrene Coolers: Must be free of all food residue, plastic handles, metal hinges, cold packs, tape, labels, and stickers.Polystyrene Packing Blocks & Sheets: Must be free of moisture, dirt, cardboard, tape, labels, plastic film, or any other debris.Packing Peanuts \(All Colors\): Must be clean, dry, and reusable. They must be bagged or boxed separately and cannot be mixed with block foam. ⚠️ Important Handling Note: Please keep pieces as whole as possible. Do not break foam into small pieces. Excessively broken material is difficult to inspect, often hides contaminants, and may be rejected. It is not cost-effective to test numerous small fragments. We WILL NOT ACCEPT: Broken/Diced Foam: If your foam is broken into many small pieces \(beyond one or two breaks per original block\), it will be rejected. Do not break up and bag your foam to "save space." \#7 "Biodegradable" or Starch-Based Foam: This is not polystyrene. It can be disposed of in your regular trash or dissolved in water. \#5 Polypropylene Foam: A less common packing foam that is brittle and breaks when bent. It is frequently misidentified and does not react to the same recycling process as polystyrene. Any material with tape, labels, plastic film, dirt, food residue, or moisture. $5 per standard trash bag-sized load of accepted material. This helps cover the cost of transportation and processing. All accepted material will be transported to our local recycling center for proper densification and recycling.Thank you for your understanding and cooperation. By ensuring your foam is clean and contaminant-free, you are directly contributing to a successful recycling program. Thank you for taking the time to recycle your polystyrene foam correctly. For this program to be successful, it is extremely vital that the material we collect is COMPLETELY free of contaminants. We cannot accept "mostly clean" or material you "think is clean." Our processor has zero tolerance for contamination.Why is this so strict? During the recycling process, the foam is melted and densified. Any plastic, especially from tape, will ruin an entire batch.A single piece of tape can contaminate up to 100 lbs of melted polystyrene, forcing the entire load to be landfilled. This negates the recycling efforts of everyone who participated correctly. Your meticulous care is what makes this program sustainable.

events.summary: Portland, clear the afternoon. Phuture Phunk is taking over the White Owl Social Club patio for seven hours of bass, color, tropical heat, spacey sounds, and seriously funky grooves. DJ Spun brings decades of dancefloor experience from San Francisco to New York, joined by DJ Dazy, Funkhouser, and Kepi for a lineup built to keep things moving from the first record to the final beat. Saturday, September 5 2 PM–9 PM White Owl Social Club 1305 SE 8th Ave, Portland 21+ $13 presale | $20 at the door Come early, bring your people, and step into the Phuture Phunk. ARTIST SPOTLIGHT: DJ SPUN Raised on Bay Area punk, hip-hop, disco, house, acid, and the early San Francisco rave scene, DJ Spun has never stayed inside one musical lane. He began DJing in the late 1980s before becoming a major presence in New York’s underground dance community. Along the way, he founded Rong Music, helped bring disco edits to new generations of American dancefloors, and spent seven years curating music for MoMA PS1’s Warm Up series. Expect a set shaped by decades of digging, editing, experimenting, and knowing exactly when to take the dancefloor somewhere unexpected. ARTIST SPOTLIGHT: DJ DAZY DJ Dazy is a Los Angeles-based house DJ known for her deep, soulful, and funky sound, rooted in a lifelong connection to vinyl culture. She began DJing in 1991, often as the only female DJ in her scene, and went on to help shape West Coast house music through the 90s and early 2000s, including founding the female DJ collective Sister DJs. With over three decades behind the decks, her style is defined by warm basslines, musical storytelling, and an intuitive ability to read a dance floor. Whether opening a room or taking it deeper into the night, she creates a journey that feels both effortless and intentional. After stepping back for a period, DJ Dazy returned to the scene in 2024 with a renewed energy, blending her original vinyl roots with a modern digital setup. Since then, she has been actively playing across Los Angeles and beyond, sharing lineups with respected artists and reconnecting with the community that shaped her. Her sets move between deep house, soulful grooves, disco influences, and classic cuts from her extensive record collection, always focused on feeling over hype. Equally comfortable on vinyl or digital, she brings a level of experience and authenticity that comes from decades of dedication to the craft.

Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. events.summary: What does it mean to lead, to worship, or to seek perfection — especially when the mirror keeps changing shape? In Take Me to Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown, Corean-born, Pacific Northwest–based performance artist Monel Chang (aka Moldy Melon) dives headfirst into a kaleidoscopic exploration of beauty, power, and the absurd rituals of becoming. Part pansori opera, part clown confession, part K-beauty séance, this solo performance unfolds like a fever dream across three acts. We meet a traditional pansori singer, steeped in ancient song and wonder; a K-beauty devotee, consumed by an altar of serums, snails, and sheet masks; and a self-proclaimed dictator, leading a birthday party for themself with military precision and toddler rage. Each character teeters between the sacred and the ridiculous, revealing how rituals of transformation — whether spiritual, aesthetic, or political — can both liberate and imprison us. Through meticulous physicality, voice, and gesture, Chang conjures a world where skincare becomes salvation, laughter becomes resistance, and a dictator’s parade dissolves into a child’s tantrum. With cues of light, sound, and scent, the stage transforms into a surreal landscape of shifting identities — from vanity table to battlefield, from face mask to flag. At once hilarious and haunting, The Seoul of a Clown interrogates the myth of perfection — in beauty, in heritage, and in leadership — while celebrating the messy, clownish heart that beats beneath it all. Drawing from Korean folk traditions, contemporary clowning, and the heightened absurdity of global pop culture, Chang builds a world where the search for “flawless skin” mirrors the search for self, and where even dictators might cry under their makeup. The result is a sensorial and spiritual satire — a ritual of laughter, longing, and self-recognition. Whether you leave glowing, weeping, or simply moisturized, Take Me to Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown promises an unforgettable night at the edge of comedy and catharsis.
events.title: Take Me To Your Leader: The Seoul of a Clown

events.summary: Balkan Bump is the global electronic music project orchestrated by trumpet player, producer and ethnomusicologist Will Magid. Balkan Bump’s music fuses heavy electronic production with global music influences including traditional Balkan brass melodies, Middle Eastern sounds and American hip hop. The Balkan Bump live show highlights Magid’s expertise as an orchestrator, ranging in size from a solo performer to a 12-piece band featuring a menagerie of global instruments including sitar, saz, oud, clarinet and trumpet. The live performance’s popularity has brought the project to global renown with performances at the world’s biggest music stages including Coachella, Bonnaroo and Lightning In A Bottle, as well as beloved jazz, blues and world music festivals including Harvest Music Festival and CA WorldFest, and numerous appearances at Colorado’s famed Red Rocks Amphitheatre. Balkan Bump debuted with the single “Aymo” alongside famed Slovenian producer Gramatik and American hip hop royalty Talib Kweli. Gramatik quickly championed the new project, unveiling Balkan Bump's live show on his Re:Coil Tour and releasing Balkan Bump’s debut EP on his Lowtemp label imprint. Since then the Balkan Bump project has gone on to collaborate with global and live music projects Beats Antique and Moon Hooch; international electronic music superstars CloZee, Fakear, & Manic Focus; and American hip hop icon The Gift Of Gab (Blackalicious). Balkan Bump has been featured in Billboard Magazine, NPR’s The World, The San Francisco Chronicle and Magnetic Magazine. In 2020 Magid curated a series of global music mixes for Los Angeles-based Dublab Radio under the Balkan Bump alias. As a solo artist, Will Magid has collaborated and performed with artists including Bonobo, Erykah Badu, Pretty Lights, and soul music legend Solomon Burke. He has led numerous jazz and global music outfits including his eponymous soul-funk band’s seminal Alligator Spacewalk album in 2016, and the 2017 neoclassical exploration Lunar Conquest Suite. His music has been featured in campaigns for global brands including Warner Brothers, Uber, Porsche, HP, Vogue, GoPro and Ubisoft. Magid graduated from The UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music with a degree in Ethnomusicology.

events.summary: TICKETS truewest.info/WITCH26 On Sale Friday, June 5 at 10am PT This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- A pioneering Zambian psychedelic act, W.I.T.C.H. \(the name is an acronym, standing for We Intend to Cause Havoc\) were one of the defining acts of Zamrock, a fusion of Western rock and rhythm & blues with traditional African sounds. They were among Zambia's most popular and influential bands in the 1970s as a wave of psychedelic and hard rock gained an audience in Africa. A landlocked nation in the South of Africa, Zambia was formerly Northern Rhodesia until gaining its independence in 1964, and as Zambia established its own national identity, local musicians began embracing the progressive influences of artists such as the Beatles, the Rolling Stones, and Jimi Hendrix, as well as the forward-thinking soul and funk sounds of James Brown. By the mid-'70s, Zambia was falling into political chaos as the nation's once-profitable mining industry ran dry, and many Zamrock bands reflected this with a darker, more psychedelic influenced sound that suggested a familiarity with the likes of Deep Purple and Grand Funk Railroad. W.I.T.C.H.'s 1972 debut, Introduction, was the first commercial album released by a Zambian band, and they continued to deliver music until fading into dormancy in the mid-'80s. A reissue campaign launched in 2011 brought the band to a new generation of listeners, and W.I.T.C.H. reunited in 2014 and started touring again shortly thereafter. In 2023, they released Zango, their first new album in almost 40 years. The original lineup of W.I.T.C.H. included vocalist Emanyeo "Jagari" Chanda, guitarists Chris Mbewe and John Muma, bassist Gedeon Mulenga, and drummer Boidi Sinkala, who were veterans of Zambian cover bands of the late '60s; Chanda \(whose nickname "Jagari" came from his fascination with Mick Jagger, one of his strongest influences\) had worked with the Red Balloons and the Boyfriends \(the latter group would evolve into another key Zamrock outfit, Peace\), while most of the other members were members of Kingston Market. . Fuelled by marijuana and Western rock and soul, the group's debut album, Introduction, was released in 1972, and was among the first commercially released LPs issued in Zambia. W.I.T.C.H.'s third album, 1975's Lazy Bones!!, is generally regarded as their finest work; while they were hampered by the primitive recording technology available in Africa, they developed a large following in Zambia and were playing stadium-sized shows throughout the continent. In the 21st century, crate diggers interested in idiosyncratic rock sounds from around the world rediscovered W.I.T.C.H., and the German reissue label Shadoks released new CD editions of Introduction and Lazy Bones!! In 2011 the American label Now Again Records released We Intend to Cause Havoc!, a comprehensive W.I.T.C.H. box set that featured their five studio albums plus a bonus collection of single tracks and unreleased material. This sparked new interest in the band, and by 2013, a Chanda-led W.I.T.C.H. with Mwondela, had regrouped and was touring again. In 2023, W.I.T.C.H. released Zango, their first album of new material in almost 40 years. It included contributions from fellow Zambian artists such as Sampa the Great . In June 2025, they released Sogolo, their second album. ~Mark Deming, Rovi

She revisited her upbringing in St. Louis, and decided to make “iPod music” — a free-for-all of feral punk, corroded pop, and raunchy rap — conjuring the “Midwest-core tweaker bar rat” characters of her youth. This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- Southern Culture On The Skids has been consistently recording and touring around the world since 1983. The band \(Rick Miller – guitar and vocals, Mary Huff – bass and vocals, Dave Hartman – drums\) has been playing together for over 30 years. Their musical journey has taken them from all-night North Carolina house parties to late night TV talk shows \(Conan O’Brien, The Tonight Show\), from performing at the base of Mt. Fuji in Japan to rockin’ out for the inmates at North Carolina correctional facilities. They’ve shared a stage with many musical luminaries including Link Wray, Loretta Lynn, Hasil Adkins and Patti Smith. Their music has been featured in movies and TV, parodied by Weird Al, and used to sell everything from diamonds to pork sausage. In 2014 the band was honored by the Southern Folklife Collection at the University of North Carolina Chapel Hill with an exhibition featuring their music and cultural contributions. Their legendary live shows are a testament to the therapeutic powers of foot-stomping, butt-shaking rock and roll and what Rolling Stone dubbed “a hell raising rock and roll party.” At Home with Southern Culture on the Skids is the latest full length album from the band and was released in March of 2021. It was recorded during the stay at home period of the pandemic when the band was at home and not touring. The album consists of 11 tracks recorded and mixed in Rick Miller’s living room with some additional tracks recorded at his studio, The Kudzu Ranch. The first radio single off the album is “Run Baby Run”—a rocking number with deep garage roots. SCOTS bassist Mary Huff provides an urgent vocal while the band pulls back the throttle on a full race fuzz fest—cause she’s gotta to go fast! Run Baby Run! The other songs on the album are a combination of the band’s unique mix of musical genres: rock and roll, surf, folk and country—all a bit off-center, what Rick proudly calls “our wobbly Americana”. Rick goes on, “We put a few more acoustic guitars on this one, as you would expect if you recorded in your living room, but it still rocks like SCOTS. So put your headphones on, get in your favorite chair/sofa/recliner, put on “At Home With” and let’s hang out for a while.”

This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- Portland indie-rock stalwarts The Weather Machine return home this spring to celebrate the release of their fifth studio record, Love & Science Fiction, with a special hometown performance at the Aladdin Theater on May 23 rd . Recorded in Sellwood with producer Gus Berry, the album brings together the band’s signature lyrical intelligence and lush, adventurous sound. Love & Science Fiction was written by frontman Slater Smith after relocating to Wellington, New Zealand, where the songs took shape on nature walks and quiet evenings far from home. These new works are a deep and cozy exploration of spiritual bargaining, touching on themes of romance, gratitude, and letting go to examine how we use sometimes-treacherous but always-beautiful fantasies to navigate life. Over two weeks in Sellwood, Smith reunited with longtime collaborators Tim Karplus \(guitar \+ keys\), Luke Hoffman \(drums\), André Zapata \(bass\), and Noah Bernstein \(sax \+ clarinet\) to arrange and record what started out as voice memo lyrics and melodies stored on Smith's phone. The result is something special. Drawing inspiration from Joe Cocker, The Cranberries, and Andrew Bird, Love & Science Fiction feels nostalgic and modern, an album both whimsical and profound, and quintessentially Pacific Northwest. Rarely do The Weather Machine’s local members reunite in one place, making this Aladdin Theater performance a uniquely Portland moment and a celebration of enduring creative friendship. With Love & Science Fiction, the band delivers their most ambitious and heartfelt record to date – a work of imagination, gratitude, and coming home.

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: Surgical negligence under Irish law occurs when a surgeon, hospital, or other healthcare professional fails to provide the standard of care that a reasonably competent medical practitioner would have delivered in similar circumstances, resulting in avoidable harm to a patient. This can include operating on the wrong site, causing preventable surgical injuries, failing to obtain informed consent, leaving surgical instruments inside the body, or providing inadequate post-operative care. Every case is assessed on its own facts, and proving Surgical Negligence generally requires evidence showing that the accepted standard of medical care was breached and that the breach directly caused the injury. Patients may experience additional medical treatment, prolonged recovery, financial losses, or long-term physical and emotional effects because of negligent surgical care. Irish law allows eligible patients to seek compensation where negligence can be established through appropriate medical and legal evidence. Understanding your legal rights early can make a significant difference in protecting your interests and preserving important evidence. Seeking advice from experienced legal professionals helps clarify whether the circumstances meet the legal threshold for Surgical Negligence. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on representing clients in complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance throughout the legal process with a clear understanding of Irish medical negligence law. Their experience in handling surgical negligence cases helps clients understand the evidence required, the claims process, and the potential outcomes. Whether the issue involves a surgical error, delayed treatment after surgery, or another avoidable complication, obtaining informed legal advice is an important first step toward pursuing justice and fair compensation.
events.title: What is considered surgical negligence under Irish law?

events.summary: Medical experts play a crucial role in evaluating injuries that occur during assisted childbirth by carefully reviewing medical records, delivery notes, imaging scans, and the condition of both the mother and baby. They assess whether forceps, vacuum extraction, or other assisted delivery methods were used appropriately according to accepted medical standards. Specialists also examine the timing of interventions, fetal monitoring records, and whether alternative delivery options should have been considered. Their findings help determine if the injuries resulted from unavoidable complications or preventable medical negligence. In cases involving Traume from Instrumental Delivery, experts evaluate the extent of physical and neurological harm, the expected long-term impact, and the treatment or rehabilitation that may be required. They may consult with obstetricians, pediatric neurologists, radiologists, and rehabilitation professionals to provide an objective medical opinion. This expert evidence is often essential in establishing whether the standard of care fell below what would reasonably be expected. A detailed medical assessment can also help quantify the financial and personal impact of the injury, including ongoing healthcare needs and loss of quality of life. Families seeking answers often rely on experienced legal professionals to interpret these findings within the context of a compensation claim. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases, including those involving assisted childbirth injuries, and works closely with independent medical experts to build well-supported claims. By combining detailed medical evidence with legal expertise, the firm helps clients understand their rights and pursue fair compensation where negligence has contributed to avoidable birth injuries.
events.title: How do medical experts assess injuries caused by assisted childbirth?

events.summary: Proving a Surgical Negligence claim requires strong, well-documented evidence that demonstrates how a healthcare provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and caused avoidable harm. Medical records are often the foundation of the case, providing a detailed timeline of diagnosis, treatment, surgery, and follow-up care. Expert medical opinions are equally important because they help establish whether the surgeon's actions fell below the standard expected of a reasonably competent professional. Diagnostic scans, laboratory results, surgical notes, consent forms, and hospital records can further support the claim. Witness statements from medical professionals or others involved in the patient's care may also strengthen the evidence. It is essential to show not only that an error occurred but also that the mistake directly resulted in physical, emotional, or financial damage. Documentation of ongoing treatment, rehabilitation, lost income, and future medical needs can help demonstrate the full impact of the injury. Every case is unique, making a thorough investigation critical before legal proceedings begin. An experienced solicitor can identify the evidence needed, obtain independent expert reports, and build a compelling legal argument. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases and understands the detailed approach required to investigate Surgical Negligence claims. Their experience in reviewing medical evidence and working with independent experts helps clients present well-supported claims. By carefully gathering relevant documentation and establishing causation, they aim to protect the rights of individuals affected by avoidable surgical errors. Seeking legal guidance early can also help preserve important evidence and ensure procedural deadlines are met. A well-prepared case supported by credible evidence significantly improves the likelihood of achieving a fair outcome.
events.title: What evidence is required to prove a surgical negligence claim?

Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

THE EXPERIENCE Join us for a 40th anniversary screening of Sherman's March, newly restored in 4K. "Completely eye-opening for me, and for so many of us who make stories for a living." - Ira Glass "One of the best documentaries and one of the best comedies ever made." - Patton Oswalt ON SCREEN: Sherman's March 1985. Directed by Ross McElwee. Runtime: 2 hours 38 minutes. Armed with a 16mm camera and a grant to make a documentary about the lingering aftermath of William Tecumseh Sherman's 1864 march to the sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. After his girlfriend breaks up with him, Ross shifts his attention from the historical to the personal, to the battlefield of modern love, and embarks on a sociological chronicle that documents the courting rites and rituals of the New South. A generous and humanistic portrait of several remarkable women that Ross meets along the way, Sherman's March sketches its characters with novelistic sensitivity: Pat, an aspiring actress with a yen for Burt Reynolds; Claudia, a roller-skating interior designer; Jackie, the activist whose anti-nuclear advocacy dovetails with Ross's deepest fears; and above all, Charleen Swansea, Ross's mentor and a one-woman Greek chorus of unsolicited romantic counsel. A landmark of first-person filmmaking that presaged everything from Michael Moore to reality TV, Sherman's March is now available in a new 4K restoration. UNORTHODOX DO

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) in Portland, Oregon will open two new exhibitions in its Front and Center Galleries this August. tende·r·eprisal // futu·re·prise, a group exhibition of bronze works created by multiple artists through a collaborative process led by elijah jamal asani, will be featured in the Front Gallery. In the Center Gallery, large-scale wood sculptures by Philip A. Robinson Jr. will be paired with functional and sculptural ceramic works by Swapna Mukhopadhyay. Both exhibitions run August 7–September 12, 2026, with a joint reception on Thursday, August 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. elijah jamal asani, a Nigerian-American artist, convened an intergenerational group of regional Black artists to create a collection of contemporary bronze artifacts. Their work was made in response to the historic theft of the Benin Bronzes. “Dating back to the 13th century, artists from the Kingdom of Benin, which is in modern-day southern Nigeria, cast bronze into sacred altar pieces and vessels of ancestral memory,” says asani. “However, in 1897, thousands of these bronze artifacts were looted by British forces.” They have yet to be repatriated. As an act of “selfdetermined restitution,” asani worked with other Black artists to create new bronzes. MAC is honored to exhibit eleven of these sculptures, created by Adriene Cruz, Midnite Seed Abioto, Intisar Abioto, Hanifah Abioto, Vaughn Kimmons, Turiya Raiah, Nyasiah Calixte, Lea Dry, Hannah Dry, Nawens Dry, and elijah jamal asani. Swapna Mukhopadhyay creates functional and sculptural porcelain works, all hand built. “The combination of aesthetics and functionality in handmade folk artifacts has always fascinated me,” she says. “My grandmother made traditional Bengali quilts (kanthas) and wove mats for sitting on the floor (asanas). I now realize how deeply I was influenced by watching her work.” Delicate drawn elements adorn many of her ceramic surfaces, and several recent works incorporate textiles and found objects. Mukhopadhyay describes her process as “improvising around what’s available,” informed by her longtime study of ethnomathematics. A retired PSU professor, she sees mathematics as inherent to creative practice and creative expression as integral to daily life across many cultures. Her ceramic pieces are often small in scale and characterized by what she calls their “putting togetherness.” Philip A. Robinson Jr. is a sculptor and conceptual artist whose work has been exhibited nationally and internationally. Working primarily in wood and metal, Robinson creates large-scale figurative and patterned works that explore memory, structure, and identity. “My practice examines structure as a living system—how materials carry memory, how patterns encode history, and how built environments shape identity,” he explains. “Whether in wood or steel, I am asking how structure holds memory—and how we locate ourselves within it.” The exhibition will include pieces from several bodies of work, including a 42” x 61” sculpture from Welcome In, which examines belonging, and several works from The House of Regina, which honor the legacy of his late mother, Dr. Regina Arnold. Robinson holds a BFA in Studio Art from Skidmore College and an MFA in Sculpture from the Mason Gross School of the Arts at Rutgers University. The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The galleries are free and open to the public during these hours. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org

events.summary: Our Foundation series is geared towards students who are new to improvisation. Watch this 2min video from our Founder to learn more about what to expect from our classes: https://youtu.be/jbL1cooOIPA?si=WjHEZJoY7OZL05yd Our joyous & engaging classes are designed for anyone new to the practice of improvisation and for those wishing to re-learn or deepen their practice of the art form's basics. We'll learn about: 👂🏼New ways of listening 🎁 The gifts of staying in the moment 📚 Telling spontaneous stories with others 👣 Thinking on our feet & trusting our instincts 👥 Quickly collaborating with others 👀 Identifying & using non-verbal communication 💪🏼 Discovering our strengths Why Take Classes With Us? Our studio is founded on the belief that student progress only comes from providing clear instruction and feedback. We not only want our students to learn the core skills of improvisation, but we also want them to improve their skills over their time with us. Because of that, we offer learning opportunities that students won't find anywhere else. All of our students will receive the following: A safe, nurturing, and supportive environment 10 students max per class, so each gets lots of attention We offer flexible class options so students can purchase the number of classes that suits their schedule Coaching and check-ins during & after each game to help make sure you've understood the breakthroughs Blackboard discussions during class, when necessary, to help visual and analytical learners Closing every class with students recognising their own wins Receiving highly personalised notes via email from your teacher, celebrating your wins during the class series & recommending skills to work on when you come back for another class with us. events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/Pond26 On Sale Friday, April 10 at 10am PT ---------------------------------------- Pond offer a skerrick of hope in a hostile world with a new record - their 11th - Terrestrials. A cyclone of urgent, scorched earth rock’n’roll, Terrestrials tips the hat to the sounds of then while squarely facing up to the here and now. Conceived from a place of reverence for a particularly potent epoch in Oz rock, Terrestrials mines the sound of open sky melancholia, heat haze sizzling on the plains and jangly pub backrooms that hits an eternally poignant nerve for anyone familiar with the sound, time and place. From there Terrestrials evolved and the idea of “Goths at the pub” became the record’s stylistic north star - iconic 80s Australiana being acid-washed with the eyeliner-stained post-punk of Sisters Of Mercy, Magazine and the like. Reverb-y drum machines, Roland JC50 amps, flanger fx, 12-string acoustics through icy amps and plenty of chorus. Sinuous and propulsive, hard and fast, edgy and expansive, between taut, trim verses and sprawling, soaring choruses, Terrestrials emerged. “Would Goths like it?” “Could you have a beer to this?” If the answers were yes it was thrust into the mix. For the first time in Pond history, the recording process was subject to a simple set of rules that concentrated sessions and accounts for the albums airtight palette and consistently buzzed energy levels. Namely - No fuzz pedal. No ballads. No “Pink Floyd shit”. Relishing the restrictions rather than overdubbing to infinity, the resultant work was reportedly the breeziest Pond record to make, and arguably the bands most focused. Terrestrials originated in 2025 at the Pond studio in Fremantle, Dream Dust 2. Finally having access to a space of their own that was big enough to set up in and leave it that way, varying combinations of band members dropped by to write and record live to tape at their leisure. With the bones of the record established, the band decamped for ten days to a rented plasterboard shack next to a limestone block pub in an end of the earth-style town called Seabird \(“The most West Australian place you could ever imagine”\) to iron things out between bouts of daytime TV and band meetings in the pub next door. An additional three tracks were put down during some tour downtime at Nowave Studios in Mullumbimby, NSW, and another two were finished back at Tuna Fish in Fremantle. Like much of the Pond catalogue, Terrestrials is a record of people and place, of exploring the identity of each, as well as where and how they intersect and interact. Extractive capitalism, power dynamics, inequality, indigenous incarceration, eccentric outcasts, fire and water, diesel and dust, unity and division, blood and bauxite, unborn tomorrows and dead yesterdays - it’s all there. Terrestrials twitches with the desperation of people and planet on the brink, but ultimately bets on the beauty of both to prevail. Pond is Nick Allbrook, Jay Watson, Joe Ryan, Jamie Terry, James Ireland. Terrestrials was produced by Pond, mixed by Jay Watson and James Ireland.
